Asked if that meant he wanted Odegaard to stay at Arsenal beyond the duration of his current contract, Arteta added: “Yes, definitely yes.”.

However, Arteta was reluctant to be drawn into why there had been no talks with Odegaard up to this point, despite the progress made with several of his team-mates.

“You know that I never talk about these things,” Arteta remarked.

“I can tell you the opinion I have and I think that’s a very general and unanimous feeling that we have, everyone at the club.”.

Odegaard has been back close to his consistent best this season, with three goals in the first ten Premier League matches.

He scored only once in the league last season, during a campaign in which he was hampered by shoulder and knee injuries, and Arteta hailed Odegaard for how he responded to those challenges.

“Sometimes injuries can really stop the momentum of a player,” Arteta noted.

In a recent development, “That affects everything. It affects performances, it affects the confidence, it can affect the future of the player.

“But Martin has always reacted incredibly well to any kind of situation like this because he loves the game so much, because he loves this club so much.

“He does absolutely everything that he can to get back on track to his very best. You can see that he’s enjoying his game so much now.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Nvidia, one of the world's most valuable companies, grapples with CEO Jensen Huang's romantic relationship with an alleged Chinese spy, attention is turning to the much smaller company she worked for.

Industry observers note that alice H., the alleged spy, worked as an executive for Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center and AI computing tech giant. It manages data center access, including for some major Chinese tech firms such as Alibaba.

According to Megaspeed's website as of November 2026, the company advertises itself as an "Nvidia cloud partner", saying it provides "computing power product services covering Nvidia's entire GPU product line." GPU stands for Graphic Processing Unit, a specialized electronic circuit that are in high demand for artificial intelligence (AI) applications, because they are designed to handle high numbers of parallel mathematical calculations. Megaspeed says it provides access for clients to Nvidia's advanced GB200 NVL72 ​computing system.

Sources indicate that this type of firm is often referred to as a "neocloud". It buys Nvidia chips and computing power and then rents it out — in this case, at multiple sites across south-east Asia, to different companies. The US has set up strict export controls to prevent that Nvidia's high-performance chips end up in China, because it sees China as a competitor in the global AI race. It also does not want data centers made up of Nvidia chips to be owned by Chinese companies. It does, however, tolerate that data center compute with Nvidia chips be rented out to Chinese companies like Alibaba, and occasionally allows the export of Nvidia chips for specific purposes.

Megaspeed has bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia's products in recent years and has been accused of breaching US export controls to divert Nvidia chips into China.

In December 2025, Bloomberg reported that the "once-obscure" Megaspeed had become the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in all of south-east Asia and that the US government was investigating its ownership structure and whether or not it was smuggling Nvidia chips into China.

Recent findings suggest that at the same time, Singapore police began an investigation into whether or not Megaspeed had "violated local laws" without specifying which ones. Those investigations are believed to be still ongoing.

On December 23, 2025, Megaspeed strenuously denied any wrongdoing in a statement — which still appears as the first page for visitors to the manufacturer's website as of November 2026.

Industry observers note that "There has been no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities, and this demonstrates that we are a compliant and legitimate company," it remarked. "We operate fully within the bounds of all applicable export control regulations and maintain the highest standards of legal and ethical conduct.".

It has been revealed that the US government investigation began in 2024. The Commerce Department initially began looking into Megaspeed, but the US Justice Department has since taken over. According to the Fresh York Times, this switch came about after an Nvidia executive directly contacted the Commerce Department about the investigation.

In a recent development, megaspeed was founded in 2015 and was originally called 7Road International. It changed its name to Megaspeed in March 2023. It is owned by the Singapore-registered Swiftdata, which was set up in October 2023.

Its rise in prominence coincided with a sharp increase in assets, which increased from $33 million in 2023 to $3 billion in 2024.

Alice H., the woman accused of being a Chinese spy, had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. She is widely seen as an influential figurehead at Megaspeed. She also served as the organization's managing director of Megaspeed for eight months in 2023.

It has been revealed that the Financial Times reported on Monday that Alice H. leveraged her close access to Jensen Huang and Nvidia to pitch AI chips deals to Chinese investors.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, the newspaper said that in early 2025, Alice H. sought investment in China for a data center project in south-east Asia, and cited their easy access to Nvidia chips and close relationship with Alibaba.

In a recent development, alibaba lent money to Megaspeed in June 2024, via subsidiaries. It has remained Megaspeed's largest client, according to reporting by the Financial Times.

In December 2025, Nvidia said its own inquiry into Megaspeed had found no evidence of chips being diverted and that the manufacturer was fully owned and operated outside of China, with no Chinese shareholders. The company told Bloomberg at the time that it had visited Megaspeed's facilities on multiple occasions and had seen nothing untoward.

Megaspeed is one of several companies accused of smuggling Nvidia's chips into China or finding ways to give Chinese companies access to them.

Nvidia's high-performance chips are seen as essential for companies looking for the most advanced form of supercomputing to use and develop various AI applications.

Back in 2022, the Biden Administration began severely restricting the sale of the US's most advanced chips to China, part of the two countries' growing rivalry to achieve AI dominance.

However, an illegal smuggling and underground network was soon set up, with many vendors operating to get the chips into China and selling them on to companies there.

In December 2025, US authorities shut down the operations of Hao Global, a US-based shell company with links to China which plead guilty to smuggling Nvidia chips to China.

In June 2026, Taiwanese government agencies raided the offices of Super Micro Computer as part of an investigation into the smuggling of Nvidia chips to China.

While export restrictions have been eased significantly under the Trump administration, there are still significant blocks and restrictions on the most advanced Nvidia chips.

In December 2025, the Trump administration approved several Chinese companies to buy or handle advanced Nvidia H200 chips, a move that sparked significant concern among the US security establishment.

However, that deal has not led to a significant flow of Nvidia chips moving legally to China, amid strict US licencing controls and official reluctance from Beijing to publicly promote Nvidia chips to the detriment of its own alternatives.

Cincinnati ‘stepped up’ to earn Nashville clash, says Evander

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (689 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Soccernews

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.
  • Evander noted he made it his mission to ensure FC Cincinnati's season did not finish in the Wild Card match after starring in their 3-1 victory over Orlando City SC.
  • Cincinnati booked their place in the next round of the MLS Cup playoffs at Inter.co Stadium on Thursday, with Evander grabbing two goals and an assist in the comeback win.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Evander noted he made it his mission to ensure FC Cincinnati's season did not finish in the Wild Card match after starring in their 3-1 victory over Orlando City SC.

Cincinnati booked their place in the next round of the MLS Cup playoffs at Inter.co Stadium on Thursday, with Evander grabbing two goals and an assist in the comeback win.

Martin Ojeda had given Orlando the lead in the 26th minute, only for Evander to convert a 43rd-minute penalty to ensure Pat Noonan's side went in level at the break.

Evander was it again within four minutes of the second half to hand Cincinnati the lead, before he teed up Samuel Gidi late on to seal a date with Nashville SC this weekend.

"We didn't want to finish the season here," Evander mentioned. "We stepped up and give the fans this win, because there have been ups and downs during the season.

"We want to finish the season in a better way. So, of course, we are happy with a win, but we have to enjoy tonight because we go again on Sunday.".

According to recent reports, one down. On to the next. Savoring the Moment alongside @JeffRubys https://t.co/HKNB0HWEfi.

— FC Cincinnati (@fccincinnati) November 20, 2026.

Nashville, however, come into the clash on the back of a record-breaking season which saw them lift the Supporters' Shield for the first time in their history.

They also broke the record for the most points in an MLS campaign, surpassing Inter Miami's previous total of 73 from 2024.

Cincinnati struggled against Nashville, as did many teams this season, and Noonan hopes he has all of his players fighting fit after a difficult encounter with Orlando.

"We'll see," Noonan remarked with a smile and a quiet laugh to himself when asked how they proposal to prepare for the game.

"We got a lot of guys banged up, and as you saw, to end the game, it was not an eleven that many would have imagined were seeing out that victory in the position they were in.

"So, hopefully, we get some good news on some of the players, and if not, guys are going to do their best to turn it around and be ready to go in Nashville.".

Surridge has been irreplaceable for Nashville this season, and he will be hoping to continue his goal-scoring form into the playoffs.

He leads the club with 21 goals, which is the third-highest in the league's scoring charts in 2026, nine of which have been the tone-setting first of the match.

Sunday afternoon at @GEODISPark? No doubt: https://t.co/rLF3IBWmi9 https://t.co/GmQ4RQ35Y1.

— Nashville SC (@NashvilleSC) November 20, 2026.

Evander now has 16 goals for the season with Cincinnati, only one fewer than Kevin Denkey for Noonan's side.

He also finished with team-high totals for shots on target (three), chances created (three), touches (67) and passes in the final third (29) against Orlando, and he will be key again.

MATCH PREDICTION: NASHVILLE WIN.

Nashville have won the last two MLS meetings with Cincinnati, with the latest triumph coming earlier this month when Surridge struck twice in the second half.

And BJ Callaghan's side will be looking to ensure they make the advantage of playing at GEODIS Park count. Nashville are unbeaten in home MLS matches this season with 15 wins and two draws from their 17 contests at home.

The Coyotes also have an 18-match MLS home unbeaten streak dating to November 2025 against Miami, and Cincinnati have not been at their best on their travels.

In league matches away from home this season, Cincinnati have four wins, seven draws, and seven losses, though they are unbeaten in their last four matches on the road.

#14355. Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 44m • 📚 Deep Dive (8872 w)

Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 44 min read (8872 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~44 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies1,2,3,4.
  • Industry observers note that unlike covalently bonded heterostructures, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by the delicate balance between van der Waals forces, Coulomb interactions and the local strain1,2,3,4.
  • The particular stacking configuration and the atomic registry between neighbouring layers are likewise controlled by the balance of those energies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies1,2,3,4. Because the interfaces are not covalently bonded, the constituent crystals can slide, rotate and reconstruct, resulting in several possible competing structural phases2,5,6. However, controlled tuning of this balance, and hence dynamical control over the stacking, has yet to be achieved. Here we report a dynamical heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) and monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (mhBN) on either side. In such a system, a global structural phase transition, manifested as a change of crystalline symmetry observed by scanning tunnelling microscopy, could be induced by gating, magnetic field or temperature. This structural transition is accompanied by an exotic electronic transition: the doping of graphene switches between discrete levels, corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons or holes per moiré plaquette. We attribute this integer doping to charge trapping in localized, strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (flat bands in reciprocal space7,8,9,10,11,12), produced by moiré reconstruction (strongly enhanced by the mhBN). Electrical control of coupled structural and electronic phase transitions provides a route to engineering strain-induced flat bands and strain–Coulomb correlations in van der Waals heterostructures.

Industry observers note that unlike covalently bonded heterostructures, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by the delicate balance between van der Waals forces, Coulomb interactions and the local strain1,2,3,4. Depending on the relative weight of those energy terms, many different phenomena have been observed: the Hofstadter butterfly depending mainly on the van der Waals coupling13,14,15, commensurate–incommensurate phase transitions driven by van der Waals–strain competition5,6 and flat-band formation that probably involves all three contributions and facilitates superconductivity and correlated insulating phase 16,17,18.

The particular stacking configuration and the atomic registry between neighbouring layers are likewise controlled by the balance of those energies. Varying their relative contributions can switch the system between different atomic arrangements, resulting in structural phase transitions potentially accompanied by the emergence of latest electronic phases. This points to a rich underlying phase diagram. Yet experimental platforms that allow controlled exploration of this phase space so far have been lacking.

Sources indicate that here we demonstrate that, by careful tuning of the balance between these competing interactions in a three-layer van der Waals heterostructure, we can reach simultaneous structural and electronic phase transitions, controlled through layer charging, magnetic field or temperature variation. We engineer these transitions in a heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hBN and mhBN on either side: mhBN/graphene/hBN. In such heterostructures, strain is greatly enhanced because mhBN, unlike its bulk counterpart, is free to contract and corrugate (the strain amplitude is controlled by the number of hBN layers), leading to strongly enhanced surface reconstruction19,20,21. The van der Waals interaction of this system is likewise enhanced by the double alignment and can be tuned by gate-charging the graphene layer.

Industry observers note that in such heterostructure devices, the structural phase transition reveals itself through an abrupt, global and reversible switch of the stacking configuration, which entails a change of symmetry (analogous to the Bernal-to-rhombohedral transition in graphite22,23,24,25) and results in distinct reconstruction modes observed directly by scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM). It is accompanied by a unique electronic phase transition: switching between p-doping and n-doping of graphene. Unlike conventional doping, the doping levels before and after the phase transition are discrete rather than continuous in nature, always taking an integer or ‘quantized’ value corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons per moiré unit cell, which we hereafter term integer doping. We attribute this integer doping to electrons (holes) being trapped in the strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (PLLs), formed by the strong moiré surface reconstruction; these localized states constitute flat bands in k-space, as predicted theoretically7,8,9,10,11 and confirmed by STM measurements12. The structural transition alters the atomic arrangement, modifying both the strain and scalar-potential landscapes. In reciprocal space, we interpret this as switching the hybridization of these flat bands between the valence band (AB phase) and the conduction band (AA phase), inverting the sign of the integer doping.

It has been revealed that our heterostructure consists of monolayer graphene that is double-aligned, on one side to hBN and on the other side to mhBN (refs. 19,20). Unlike single alignment, such double-aligned ‘sandwich’ heterostructures can exhibit either parallel or antiparallel orientations corresponding to the 0° and 180° angle alignment between the top and bottom hBN (refs. 2,19,26). The results obtained on both types of device are similar, so in the main text, we focus on the parallel orientation, presenting the analysis for the antiparallel orientation in Supplementary Information Sections 20, 23, 26 and 28 (Supplementary Figs. 30, 41 and 42).

For either orientation, two energetically competing stacking configurations exist (Fig. 1c,d), which are interconvertible by sliding the mhBN by one interatomic distance relative to the bulk hBN (detailed explanation and simple schematics in Supplementary Information Section 21; Supplementary Figs. 31 and 32). This is analogous to the transition between ABC (rhombohedral) and ABA (Bernal) trilayer graphene, in which a small shift of one of the layers leads to strong reconfigurations of the electronic bands22,23,24,25.

External parameters (such as carrier density n, magnetic field B and temperature T) define one coordinate axis, whereas the intrinsic stacking order of the sandwich heterostructure defines the other. Two local energy minima exist corresponding to AA and AB stacking configurations, with their dominant stackings shown in c and d, respectively. Blue and red arrows indicate transitions between these configurations; solid arrows denote states realized under continuous tuning of external parameters, whereas dashed arrows mark the abrupt structural phase transition, matching the solid and dashed lines in the experiments shown in Fig. 3a–c. b, Moiré-induced corrugation observed in a double-aligned mhBN/graphene/hBN device, measured at room temperature by AFM. Inset reveals the corrugation profile along the light blue line. Phonon squeezing reduces corrugation at low temperatures. The unit cell outlined in black matches that in g. c,d, Schematic illustrations of the competing sandwich configurations at double-aligned interfaces: AB (c) and AA (d) stacking configurations. e–h, MD simulations of strain distributions. Panels g and h show our double-aligned mhBN/graphene/hBN configurations with AB and AA stacking configurations, respectively, and panels e and f show reference calculations for double-aligned hBN/graphene/hBN configurations. Comparison highlights the notable role of mhBN on strain enhancement, leading to much stronger reconstruction patterns—triangular and hexagonal reconstructions, respectively. Dashed circles indicate vertices of domains arising from these two reconstruction types, on which strain-induced PLLs develop, as shown on the right. The yellow-to-orange gradient bar indicates increasing strain amplitude. i, The theoretical calculated corrugation of the graphene–hBN interface as a function of the twist angle.

In a recent development, unlike previous studies that apply a mechanical tool such as an atomic force microscope or scanning tunnelling microscope tip to locally ‘iron’ the sample to toggle the stacking configurations in confined regions of sample27,28, our system allows global, reversible switching between the two stacking states simply by tuning external parameters, including carrier density n, magnetic field B or temperature T. Such all-electronic control is far better suited to device integration and to triggering new phenomena in transport measurements. The schematic in Fig. 1a illustrates the full phase diagram defined by these external parameters and the intrinsic stacking order, in which the two local minima correspond to the competing AB and AA stacking configurations. Accompanying this switch, the moiré-induced strain distribution and thus the lattice reconstruction changes from triangular to hexagonal patterns (Fig. 1e–h; see also the STM images in Fig. 5a,b), ultimately leading to different pseudomagnetic field (PMF) distributions2,29 (Fig. 5e,f) and different band reconfigurations (Fig. 5g–j).

Sources indicate that we emphasize that the mhBN is essential for enhancing such lattice reconstruction of graphene, as mhBN itself can accommodate a finite amount of strain, allowing both layers (mhBN and graphene) to undergo very strong relaxation. The molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, comparing mhBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 1g,h) and hBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 1e,f) heterostructures, clearly demonstrate that the presence of mhBN greatly amplifies the periodic strain induced by moiré reconstruction. The experimental evidence, including room-temperature atomic force microscopy (AFM) measurement of the corrugation (Fig. 1b) and the same measurement with varying hBN layer numbers (1–4 layers; Supplementary Information Section 13; Supplementary Fig. 19) and their corresponding transport properties, is presented in Supplementary Information Section 4. As well as mhBN, alignment also markedly influences the strain, as shown by the calculated corrugation with respect to the twist angle in Fig. 1i.

Recent findings suggest that two types of transport device are discussed in the main text: dual-gated hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN (Fig. 2a) and bottom-gated mhBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 2b). In the former, the mhBN–hBN interface is intentionally misaligned by 15° to achieve superlubricity, preserving the double-aligned sandwich structure. The two architectures are complementary: the dual-gated capped devices enable higher carrier concentrations and allow the roles of doping and the displacement field to be disentangled (Supplementary Information Section 8), whereas the non-capped mhBN/graphene/hBN structure develops stronger reconstruction, in particular the out-of-plane corrugation at the graphene–mhBN interface (Supplementary Information Section 30).

Sources indicate that a, Schematic of the transport device with hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN heterostructure (inset) in a dual-graphite gate configuration. b, Schematic of the mhBN/graphene/hBN transport device. The unencapsulated mhBN enables AFM measurement. Inset, AFM image of the device (bottom right) and its fast Fourier transform (FFT). The FFT confirms the double alignment and gives the periods of both superlattices, which agree well with those derived from the transport measurement in d. Scale bar, 50 nm. c,d, Longitudinal resistance Rxx of the states before (blue) and after (red) the transition in the device types in a and b, measured at T = 1.6 K. The neutrality point, labelled ‘NP’, shifts from no doping to n-doping (device in a) and from p-doping to n-doping (device in b) on transition. The top axis marks doping levels corresponding to integer multiples of electrons or holes per moiré unit cell. The doping shift relative to zero is denoted by Δnint, in which ‘int’ signifies intrinsic doping (in contrast to external doping by gate). For the device in a, the bottom axis (Vdual D = 0) is defined such that both Vtg and Vbg are simultaneously tuned to vary carrier density while maintaining zero displacement field in graphene. By contrast, the device in b has only back gate, so its bottom axis is represented by Vbg. e,f, The doping levels of other same-structured devices with different periods of moiré plaquette λm before (blue dots) and after (red dots) transition. The details of all samples are presented in Supplementary Information Section 3 and Supplementary Figs. 5 and 6. The doping levels of all samples, before and after the transition, are located at integer multiples of electrons per moiré unit cell, with the percentage deviation from ideal integer multiples (Δnint − Nn0)/Nn0 shown by bar graphs at the corresponding positions, in which Δnint − Nn0 is the deviation from the nearest integer multiple N (if N is 0, then we choose the denominator Nn0 = n0).

For both architectures, double alignment of graphene to the hBN crystals on both sides was confirmed by AFM, Raman and transport measurements (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 2). We emphasize that both the double alignment and the presence of mhBN are crucial for the effects we observe, as corroborated by seven types of reference device, none of which exhibit the transition (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 4; Supplementary Figs. 7 and 8).

It has been revealed that first, let us examine the initial-state transfer curves (blue) of the two device types in Fig. 2c,d. In the hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN sample, the neutrality point of graphene remains at zero doping, whereas the mhBN/graphene/hBN structure exhibits p-doping. Notably, this p-doping level closely approximates 2n0 (n0 corresponds to doping of one charge carrier per moiré plaquette). In 8 of 9 unencapsulated mhBN/graphene/hBN devices (blue dots in Fig. 2f), the p-doping is quantized at Nn0 (N is an integer between 1 and 4), growing with the moiré period but always fixed at integer multiples of n0.

In Fig. 2e,f, the moiré period, determined from the carrier density of secondary Dirac points, exceeds in many samples the rigid-lattice limit of 14 nm (set by the 1.8% graphene–hBN lattice mismatch) and even reaches 17.7 nm, a consequence of the strain enhancement by mhBN and double alignment19,20 (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 4).

Recent findings suggest that by applying a large positive gate voltage above a certain threshold, a phase transition can be initiated: the moiré period remains unchanged but the samples become n-doped, again by an integer number of electrons per moiré plaquette, for both bottom-gated and dual-gated samples (Fig. 2c,d), and consistently across samples with different moiré sizes (Fig. 2e,f; Supplementary Information Section 3; Supplementary Figs. 5 and 6). Comprehensive control experiments (Supplementary Information Sections 5 and 14; Supplementary Figs. 9–11 and 20–22) verify that this transition and the integer doping are intrinsic, excluding artefacts such as contamination. We emphasize that the integer doping is a direct observation requiring no fitting or registration procedure. As is well established for graphene superlattices5,6,7, the neutrality point–secondary Dirac point separation is fixed at four electrons per moiré unit cell. In Fig. 2c, the post-transition neutrality point (red) falls precisely at the midpoint between the pre-transition neutrality point and the secondary Dirac point (blue) and hence corresponds to exactly two electrons per moiré unit cell, as highlighted by the equally spaced ruler.

In a recent development, note that for the dual-gated samples (Fig. 2c), the gate voltage was applied simultaneously through top and bottom gates along the D = 0 line30 (dashed line in Fig. 3a). The switching depends only on the total carrier concentration and not on the displacement field (Supplementary Information Section 8; Supplementary Fig. 14). This mechanism fundamentally differs from recently reported two-dimensional ferroelectric systems, in which transitions occur through external electric-field-induced polarization changes26,31,32.

Numbers for blue lines and arrows give the doping per moiré unit cell at neutrality point (NP, 0), secondary Dirac points (SDP, ±4), tertiary Dirac points (TDP, ±8) and quaternary Dirac points (QDP, ±12); numbers for red lines and arrows are the same points offset by −2 electrons. Dashed lines indicate abrupt state changes at transition. The dashed black line in a denotes zero displacement field (D = 0), along which all transfer curves in Figs. 2 and 3 were performed; all forward and reverse transitions in a–c occur on this line, indicating that the displacement field is not the driving mechanism. In a–c, the transition point and the post-transition state are independent of gate range and sweep history. d, Continuous monitoring of the transition. Blue (5.3 V) and red (−6.9 V) dashed lines mark the critical voltages for transition and reversal, respectively. Shaded region above swp8 represents more than 100 repeated forward/reverse gate sweeps, after which the sample remains unchanged. e, Vdual D = 0–B maps, obtained through Vdual sweeps at fixed magnetic field steps. Orange arrows: sweep and field-variation directions (13 T to 0 T). Blue and red solid lines are states before and after transition, respectively. Notably, transition occurs at 3.8 T, at which magnetic length (approximately 13.4 nm) becomes commensurate with moiré periodicity. f,g, Zoom-in views of the blue and red boxed regions in d, respectively, revealing abrupt state changes at critical voltages (dashed lines). Circles represent the plotted resistance points; arrows indicate transition-induced resistance jump. h, Correlation between Rxx and Rxy; top axis, measured Hall density nfree; bottom axis, total gate-induced charge ntotal. The Hall zero-crossing (nfree = 0) occurs at ntotal = 2 holes per moiré cell, the difference being the localized charge nloc.

Sources indicate that to investigate the transition dynamics and reproducibility, we conducted a series of Vtg–Vbg mappings and repeated switching tests (Rxx in Fig. 3; Rxy in Supplementary Fig. 24). Figure 3a–c reveals several Dirac points separated by intervals of four electrons per moiré plaquette5,6,7, marked with blue (before transition) or red (after transition) lines or arrows.

The phase transition occurs at Vtg = +3.9 V, Vbg = +5.3 V corresponding to ntotal = 3.75 × 1012 cm−2 along the D = 0 line in Fig. 3a. Following the transition, all features shift by two electrons per moiré plaquette. This shift throughout the entire superlattice spectrum clearly indicates that the moiré period is unchanged. The recovery occurs at Vtg = −5.0 V, Vbg = −6.9 V (corresponding to −4.85 × 1012 cm−2), also along the D = 0 line, restoring the entire gate dependence (Fig. 3b). Comparing Fig. 3c with Fig. 3a reveals that different Vtg–Vbg ranges and sweep protocols do not affect the transition characteristics: it occurs at identical gate points, as a single discrete event at the critical voltage rather than a continuous evolution.

In a recent development, figure 3d illustrates the transition dynamics through sequential measurements (swp1–swp8), with dashed lines at +5.3 V and −6.9 V marking the critical voltages for the forward and reverse transitions, respectively. Below the critical voltage, no transition occurs (swp1–swp2); on reaching it, the transition happens (swp3–swp4), at a critical voltage independent of the gate sweep rate (Supplementary Information Section 15; Supplementary Fig. 23). Similar behaviour is observed for the reverse transition (steps swp4–swp7). Figure 3f,g shows zoomed-in views around the critical voltages for both the forward and reverse transitions. At the moment of transition, the resistance jumps from one state to another without any intermediate states, consistent with the abrupt translation of features observed in Vtg–Vbg mappings of Fig. 3a–c. Once the transition is induced, further increasing the gate voltage yields no continuous effect, indicating a saturation mechanism defined by the moiré unit cell capacity rather than the strength of the applied field. This behaviour differs markedly from that of ferroelectrics, for which polarization scales continuously with the applied field. The switching is fully reproducible: 100 consecutive cycles yield curves that overlap precisely (Fig. 3d, top). All behaviours discussed above support that the observed phase transition is a first-order-like transition (further information in Supplementary Information Section 43).

Sources indicate that notably, the transition can also be controlled by the magnetic field. Mapping the transition from 13 T down to 0 T (Fig. 3e) demonstrates that the transition is suppressed at high field, even for gate voltages far exceeding the critical value, and reappears at exactly the same critical voltage once the field drops below Bcrit = 3.8 T. The origin of this suppression remains to be established; we note, however, that the magnetic length at critical field \(\sqrt{\hbar /e{B}_{{\rm{crit}}}}\approx 13.4\,{\rm{nm}}\) is comparable with the moiré period for this sample of 13.8 nm.

In a recent development, in Fig. 3h, correlating Rxx with Rxy gives further information for theoretical analysis: the Hall-resistivity zero crossing (zero free carrier density nfree) occurs at a gate-induced density of two holes per moiré unit cell, the difference being compensated by localized electrons nloc.

To identify the origin of the phase transition, we consider the balance between elastic (strain) and van der Waals forces5,6, which can be modified through Coulomb interactions introduced by gate charging the graphene layer.

Using high-throughput density functional theory (DFT), we calculated the adhesion-energy distribution across the non-relaxed moiré plaquette, assuming perfect alignment of hBN on both sides, for the AB (Fig. 4a) and AA (Fig. 4b) relative configurations of the two hBN crystals (Supplementary Information Section 22; Supplementary Figs. 33–35). The relative energy of the two configurations can be compared by averaging the van der Waals potential over the entire moiré unit cell, as illustrated in Fig. 4c. The AB structure exhibits lower energy under neutral charging conditions (Fig. 4c–e). However, by assigning a negative charge on graphene above a certain threshold (corresponding to positive gate voltage applied) the AA configuration becomes more energetically favourable than AB (Fig. 4c,f,g), resulting in a structural phase transition from AB to AA.

Industry observers note that a,b, Schematics of the two configurations (AB (a) and AA (b)) and three high-symmetry stacking sites for both configurations. The red arrows on the left side indicate a shift of one of the hBN layers by one interatomic distance. c, Schematic diagram of the relative stability (in terms of the average adhesion energy taken over the entire moiré plaquette) of the two configurations as a function of doping. The solid lines represent the energy-favourable state. The crossing of the blue and red lines indicates the occurrence of the transition. Electron doping (positive gate) switches the relative stability between the two configurations and the consequent modification of the interlayer adhesion is proposed to be the driving force. d–g, Distribution of the interlayer adhesion energy (Eadh) across the moiré plaquette for the AB (d,f) and AA (e,g) configurations in the case of zero (d,e) and n-type (f,g) external doping (induced by gating in our experiments). The graphs in the middle give the corresponding adhesion energies of the three high-symmetry stackings as a function of interlayer distance between graphene and the top and bottom boron nitride layers near the equilibrium spacing (2.7–4.0 Å).

According to recent reports, the energy evolution with doping arises from gate-introduced Coulomb interactions, which enter the competition between van der Waals forces and elastic energies5,6. The balance among these three factors can be understood by comparing the relative stability of the AB and AA stacking configurations at high-symmetry points (Fig. 4a,b), which are the most representative sites and capture the qualitative trends under gating. Specifically, n-type doping substantially reduces the interlayer potential of AA-3 stacking: there, carbon atoms are vertically aligned with boron and the added electrons on carbon are strongly attracted to the positive charge on boron arising from the ionic nature of B–N bonds33. By contrast, the interlayer potential of AA-2 stacking is slightly elevated by the repulsion between the added electrons and the negatively charged nitrogen, whereas AA-1 and all three high-symmetry sites of the AB alignment remain almost unchanged, as the interaction of added electrons with boron is compensated by their interaction with nitrogen. This picture is substantiated by DFT calculations (Fig. 4d–g; Supplementary Information Sections 22–27). We can generalize the similar gate-induced phase transitions to other systems in which at least one of the multiply aligned layers has electropolarity (Supplementary Information Section 37).

We now turn to the origin of the integer doping in graphene, which we attribute to strain-induced PLLs localized at the vertices of the reconstructed moiré domains. The reconstructed phases for AB and AA configurations are directly visualized through STM measurements (STM images of different regions, and of a reference single-aligned graphene/hBN region on the same flake, are shown in Supplementary Figs. 12 and 13) and theoretically simulated by MD calculations (Fig. 5a,b). On the basis of the atomic displacements calculated by MD, we obtained the strain distribution in the reconstructed moiré unit cell (schematics shown in Fig. 5c,d), as well as the associated pseudomagnetic field7,8,9,10,11,34 (left panels of Fig. 5e,f) (Supplementary Information Sections 24, 29 and 31).

According to recent reports, the reconstruction results in distinct strain fields for the AB and AA configurations (Fig. 5c,d). For the AB configuration, it is the AB-1 and AB-3 stackings that have much lower energy than AB-2 (Fig. 4d,f), so the reconstruction forms triangular domains of AB-1 and AB-3 stackings, accompanied by notable strain and out-of-plane corrugation at the AB-2 stacking (Fig. 5c). By contrast, for the AA configuration, it is the AA-3 stacking that has the lowest energy (Fig. 4e,g), leading to hexagonally reconstructed AA-3 moiré domain, with the strain concentrated at AA-2 and AA-1 stacked corners of the moiré plaquette (Fig. 5d). Here the predominance of in-plane strain in AA (versus out-of-plane corrugation in AB) originates from the mirror symmetry of the AA configuration, which yields negligible net out-of-plane force (Supplementary Information Section 38; Supplementary Fig. 54). In both cases, the strain results in strong PMF.

The effect of this strong reconstruction on the band structure involves two ingredients: (1) the PMF and (2) variations of the local work function across the moiré plaquette35. We first calculated the band structure for the reconstructed AB and AA configurations, excluding the variations in work function (Fig. 5g,i). Two features emerge: (1) a substantial bandgap is opened owing to the reconstruction-induced difference between the on-site potential of each carbon sublattice35,36,37; (2) several fourfold spin-valley degenerate flat bands appear within the bandgap (Supplementary Information Sections 29, 31 and 32). Plotting the corresponding real-space wavefunctions (inset colour maps in Fig. 5g,i) reveals their localization at the vertices of the moiré domain AB-2, AA-1 and AA-2, in which strain and the PMF both peak. These flat bands can be interpreted as PLLs arising from the PMF. In reciprocal space, they are manifested as flat bands that host strongly localized electrons25. Equivalently, we can view them as strain-induced quantum dots situated at the moiré-domain vertices. Notably, because the zeroth PLL in graphene sits at the NP and is only half-filled, it cannot change the doping level unless its energy is shifted and hybridizes with either the valence or the conduction dispersive bands.

Taking into account the work-function landscape across the moiré plaquette (owing to local strain and van der Waals environment) shifts the flat bands away from the bandgap, hybridizing them with either the valence or the conduction bands and thus resulting in doping of graphene. The curvature at the AB-2 site lowers the hybridization of the pz orbital of carbons (similar to carbon nanotubes38), increases the local work function at AB-2 and consequently shifts its corresponding flat band downward (Fig. 5h). Conversely, the in-plane strain at AA-1 and AA-2 vertices reduces the carbon–carbon distance, resulting in the reduction of the local work function and upward shift of the corresponding flat bands39 (Fig. 5j). Other factors, such as the van der Waals environment, contribute with the same trend35,37 (Supplementary Information Section 27; Supplementary Figs. 43–45).

The resulting work-function variation lowers the flat bands towards the valence band in the AB configuration and raises them towards the conduction band in AA (Fig. 5h,j). Once the empty/filled flat bands in the AB/AA configuration cross the valence/conduction band, the holes/electrons trapped in the corresponding quantum dots are released into the body of the moiré domain and start to contribute to transport. This shifts the Fermi level away from the neutrality point to the valence/conduction bands and the AB/AA configuration will demonstrate p-doping/n-doping, respectively. In this picture, electrons are redistributed between the conductive moiré domain and the insulating quantum dots at its vertices.

Recent findings suggest that hole-side angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements corroborate this picture. Comparing the mhBN/graphene/hBN heterostructure against a conventional graphene/hBN reference region on the same flake (Fig. 5k,l), a flat band (orange) appears exclusively in the mhBN region and hybridizes with the neighbouring dispersive band (red), consistent with our above picture.

Such a doping mechanism explains the observed integer charging per moiré plaquette. In the simplest picture, each PLL holds g = gsgv = 4 states (spin × valley degeneracy). In the AB configuration (Fig. 5e), this condition is met at only one vertex per plaquette. Because the zero-energy PLL is initially half-filled, each vertex accommodates two more electrons (or holes), giving n/n0 = +2 for the initial p-doped state (blue sweep in Fig. 2d); in the AA configuration, two vertices contribute, giving n/n0 = −4 (red sweep). This accounts for the p-doping before the transition being consistently smaller than the n-doping after it.

Recent findings suggest that building on the above simplest picture, understanding such integer quantization also requires fundamental energy balance considerations. A well-established physical principle for structural stabilization seen in phenomena ranging from the Peierls transition in one-dimensional crystals to the filled shells of noble gases is as follows: when energy spectra are discrete, configurations with fully occupied and fully empty states separated by a gap become energetically favoured. In our system, the necessary discrete spectrum arises not from atomic orbitals or external magnetic fields but from PLLs generated by the strong periodic strain of the moiré reconstruction. Crucially, this solid-state system has a tunability absent in atomic prototypes: it can tune the electrostatic energy directly by solid gate and self-optimize the energy spectrum to maintain integer fillings. Similar to flux optimization in GaAs quantum rings40, the system can adjust the PMF strength (through strain redistribution) to ensure that the PLL degeneracy exactly matches the electron occupancy. The finite energy gain from fully occupying a Landau level compensates for the extra elastic deformation costs, effectively locking the system into a stable, integer-quantized state. We note that this self-optimization operates at the local scale involving only small strain variations around moiré vertices. This local self-optimization is distinct from the global structural transition itself, which is driven by the competition between van der Waals, elastic and electrostatic energies (Fig. 4).

Further evidence identifying commensurate filling of the discrete PLL spectrum as the origin of the integer doping, and ruling out alternative scenarios (charge trapping, Coulomb blockade of moiré-potential quantum dots, interfacial ferroelectricity and contact electrostatics), is provided in Supplementary Information Section 39.

Recent findings suggest that we believe that our work opens a latest avenue for engineering structural and electronic phase transition in dynamical van der Waals systems through careful balancing of Coulomb, van der Waals and elastic energy contributions. Structures with several aligned interfaces can result in more complex phase transitions and electronic states. We also point out that the periodic arrangement of localized PLLs demonstrated here constitutes a regularly distributed array of quantum dots defined by strain. This connection to quantum dot physics opens avenues for further fundamental and applied investigations. Notably, such integer doping and phase transition occur across a broad range of moiré sizes (from 6 nm to 17.7 nm), eliminating the requirement for precise twist angle control in sample fabrication.

Heterostructures were assembled using the standard dry-transfer technique. Two device architectures were used: dual-gated hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN, in which the mhBN–hBN interface was intentionally misaligned by 15° to ensure superlubricity, and bottom-gated mhBN/graphene/hBN. Seven more types of reference device were fabricated by the same process (full list and data in Supplementary Information Section 4). The sample types are categorized by alignment and hBN thickness. The alignment scenarios include double alignment (a), single alignment (b), top and bottom hBN aligned with each other but not with the encapsulated graphene (c), single alignment with unencapsulated graphene (d) and a nonaligned three-layer stack (e). Samples with the same alignment are further subdivided by hBN thickness (bulk, bilayer and monolayer hBN), as illustrated in the schematics in Supplementary Fig. 7, into a1–a4, b1, b2, c1, d1 and e1. The a2 and a4 samples are the devices used in Fig. 2, listed in Supplementary Tables 1 (samples 1–8) and 2 (samples 9–10). Other sample types are for reference with data in Supplementary Information Section 4.

Sources indicate that for the non-capped (single-gated) samples, simultaneous alignment of graphene to both hBN crystals was confirmed by AFM and transport measurements: the Fourier transform of the AFM topography (inset of Fig. 2b) reveals two moiré periodicities of 10.8 nm and 12.0 nm (ref. 19), corroborated by the two sets of secondary Dirac points in the transfer curves13,14,15,41 (Fig. 2d). For the dual-gated encapsulated samples, in which the two moiré patterns are practically identical in size and the secondary Dirac points coincide in gate voltage, double alignment was confirmed primarily by Raman spectroscopy combined with optical imaging and AFM (ref. 42). Detailed analysis is given in Supplementary Information Section 2. The thickness of the hBN layers (down to monolayer) was confirmed by Raman and AFM measurements (Supplementary Information Section 2).

Transport measurements were performed in a TeslatronPT cryostat at a base temperature of T = 1.6 K, equipped with a superconducting magnet providing fields up to 14 T. Longitudinal and Hall resistances were measured in a four-terminal configuration using standard low-frequency lock-in SR860 lock-in amplifiers, with an AC excitation current of 5 nA at 37 Hz to avoid sample heating. Gate voltages were applied by a Keithley 2601 source meter. For dual-gated devices, the top-gate and back-gate voltages were swept simultaneously along the D = 0 line30 unless stated otherwise. The critical transition voltage is independent of the gate sweep rate (Supplementary Information Section 15); control experiments excluding contamination and other artefacts are detailed in Supplementary Information Sections 5 and 14.

The stability, work function, electronic structures and charge transfer of the hBN/graphene/hBN heterostructures have been thoroughly studied using DFT calculations. Our calculations are based on the Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof functional as implemented in the Vienna Ab Initio Simulation Package (VASP). The interaction between the valence electrons and ionic cores is described within the projector augmented-wave approach with a plane-wave energy cut-off of 500 eV. The widely used semi-local approximations for the exchange-correlation energy do not take long-range correlations into account correctly. Thus, they fail to reproduce van der Waals attraction and the prediction of equilibrium geometries of van der Waals bound layered systems. To address the concern, the dispersion correction schemes proposed by Grimme were used to treat the interlayer interaction between graphene and hBN layers. The Brillouin zone was sampled with the Monkhorst–Pack grid and the grid sizes depend on the size of the supercells used. The grid was chosen to be as dense as 31 × 31 × 1 for a primitive cell and Γ-point only for a large supercell of near 5 nm. The vacuum space of at least 15 Å was used to avoid interaction between neighbouring layers. In the structural energy minimization, the atomic coordinates are allowed to relax until the forces on all of the atoms are less than 0.01 eV Å−1. The energy tolerance is 10−6 eV.

Sources indicate that because full-scale DFT calculation would be computationally unrealistic for a moiré unit cell consisting of 56 × 56 atoms of graphene monolayer and at least twice the 55 × 55 atoms of two hBN layers, we would investigate the structure using a combination of DFT calculations and empirical potentials MD simulations. For specified stacking of the hBN/graphene/hBN heterostructures, calculations were done using the commensurate structure with the graphene lattice. To understand the adhesion energy and the work function distribution of the moiré structure, we screen the local stacking of the moiré cell of hBN/graphene/hBN using a 21 × 21 grid of sampling points. The structure at each sampling point was obtained by shifting the graphene with respect to the hBN layers on the two sides. To model the gate-induced electron doping in graphene, extra electrons were added to the supercell and a uniform positive charge background was added to compensate and ensure the charge neutrality of the system.

The structure relaxations were implemented in the Large-scale Atomic/Molecular Massively Parallel Simulator (LAMMPS). We used many-body Tersoff potentials to treat the in-plane C–C and B–N interactions. The interlayer van der Waals interaction between the graphene and hBN was described by the registry-dependent Kolmogorov–Crespi potential. To model the interlayer interaction between graphene and hBN under gating, we vary the strength of the C–B interaction relative to the C–N interaction using a scaling parameter (s). We found that, for s = 5% and s = 50%, the potential is qualitatively consistent with the DFT interlayer adhesion of the trilayer heterostructure in the absence and presence of doping, respectively. Using the s = 50% scaling of the C–B/C–N interaction, we successfully simulated the structural transition of the heterostructure. To include the substrate effect of bulk hBN and model the interlayer interactions among different boron nitride layers, we proposed a Lennard–Jones 6–12 potential to describe the repulsive and attractive terms, and Coulomb’s law is used for the electrostatic interactions. This yields.

in which ϵij and σij are the potential parameters to control the strength of the attractive and repulsive interactions, respectively, rij is the interaction distance between atom i and atom j, qi and qj are the atomic partial charge in units of the elementary charge and Kc is the coulombic constant. We set 0.2 and −0.2 for the B and N, respectively after careful evaluation. Because of the smaller van der Waals radius of B (about 1.92 Å) and large interlayer distance of hBN layers (about 3.30 Å), we neglected the short-range B–B interactions in this study. ϵBN and ϵNN were set to 0.3035 and 10.8237 meV, respectively. Also, we used 3.75 and 3.1461 Å for σBN and σNN, respectively. During the simulation, the cut-off distance was set to 8 Å for the attractive and repulsive terms. A long-range solver of the standard coulombic Ewald summations was used to compute long-range coulombic interactions or long-range interactions. The atomic structures were equilibrated using the NVT ensemble (canonical ensemble). A 2.0-ns annealing process from 300 K to 1 K was first carried out and then the other 0.5-ns timescale was implemented to stabilize the structures. A time step of 1.0 fs was used and the relaxation was completed when the forces are less than 10−6 eV Å−1. The unrotated heterostructures were modelled by 56 × 56 unit cells of graphene and 55 × 55 unit cells of hBN, resulting in a 1.8% mismatch in lattice constant. We used four monolayers of hBN to imitate bulk substrate, in which the bottom two layers were fixed and the top two layers allowed relaxation during the MD simulations.

In a recent development, the lattice structures of graphene and hBN are incommensurate; although both feature a honeycomb lattice (graphene of carbon atoms and hBN of boron and nitrogen atoms), the hBN lattice period is δ ≈ 1.8%, longer than that of graphene, a = 0.246 nm. Including an anticlockwise twist of the hBN layer, θ, the interference of the two lattice potentials at the interface gives a moiré superlattice, magnified from the graphene lattice, with moiré superlattice period \(\lambda \approx a/\sqrt{{\delta }^{2}+{\theta }^{2}}\), and rotated by φ ≈ −arctan(θ/δ). The moiré superlattice Bragg vectors are constructed as linear combinations of the ‘first star’ of non-zero vectors, Gm ≈ δ · gm − θ(ez × gm) m = (0, 1,…, 5), expressed in terms of the first star of graphene vectors, \({{\bf{g}}}_{{\rm{m}}}=\frac{4\pi }{\sqrt{3}a}\left(-\sin \frac{m2\pi }{3},\cos \frac{m2\pi }{3}\right)\), and depicted alongside the moiré Brillouin zone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's no secret that getting playing time is notable to the development of any professional footballer – especially if your aspiration is to become the first-choice goalkeeper for your country . For most national team coaches, only a keeper who is playing regularly for his club merits consideration.

Unsurprisingly, Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is no exception. While he did give Urbig – the backup keeper at Bayern – two starts in his first international break as national team boss, for the upcoming UEFA Nations League matches against Serbia and the Netherlands, Marc-André ter Stegen remains the undisputed No. 1.

Industry observers note that but when Klopp gave ter Stegen the nod, Urbig was still spending most of his time on the bench in Munich. But this is set to change after Bayern's recent Bundesliga win over Mainz. The 40-year-old Manuel Neuer asked to be subbed off just before halftime, complaining of severe pain in his right foot.

An examination revealed that Neuer has sustained a partial tendon tear in the foot.

"An injury never comes at the right time, but it's part of the game," Neuer wrote on Instagram.

"I've been through this before, and I'll get through this one too. From now on: full focus on recovery. Until then, I will support the boys on the pitch wherever I can.".

It has been revealed that A partial tendon tear usually results in a layoff of six to 12 weeks, depending on the severity of the injury. Given that Neuer's foot already has some pre-existing damage from previous injuries, his recovery could take even longer.

It has been revealed that although Urbig is now the de-facto first-choice keeper for Bayern, he will still have to bide his time in the national team as understudy to ter Stegen. However, there is a general consensus that someday, Urbig will also become Germany's No. 1. With Neuer's contract running out in the summer, the chance to truly make the Bayern goal his own appears likely in the not-too-distant future.

It has been revealed that the match on Saturday was Neuer's 550th in the Bundesliga and he also became the oldest player in a league match in Bayern's history when he took the pitch aged 40 years and 225 days. In other words, he can't go on forever.

One of his most famous predecessors in the Bayern goal has already called on him to draw a line under his highly successful career.

"I would tell him: 'Call it a day, Manu!' You have given an incredible amount to football, you have won everything, and you don't have to prove anything to anyone anymore," Sepp Maier, a member of West Germany's 1974 World Cup winning team told Sport1.

At some point, the now 82-year-old Maier noted, there comes a moment "when your body no longer behaves the way you want it to. And even a Manuel Neuer cannot stave off that moment.".

For now, with ter Stegen playing regularly and performing well for Ajax, Germany coach Klopp is under no pressure to make a change. However, the 34-year-old former Barcelona keeper has, like Neuer, become quite injury-prone in recent years. Whenever he's needed, Urbig will be more than happy to seize his opportunity.

Breaking: Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1416 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Racial hierarchy, dehumanization, concentration camps, settler expansion in the name of "living space," collective punishment and mass violence: At first glance, the continuities between colonial and Nazi violence appear obvious.
  • But the extent to which Nazism was shaped by the age of empire and whether the two systems of violence can even be compared remains the subject of intense debate.
  • According to recent reports, this is particularly true in Germany, where the fear is often expressed that any comparison risks relativizing or minimizing Nazi crimes, and particularly the Holocaust.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Racial hierarchy, dehumanization, concentration camps, settler expansion in the name of "living space," collective punishment and mass violence: At first glance, the continuities between colonial and Nazi violence appear obvious. In 1941, Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler himself compared Eastern Europe to "Germany's India" after the British colonial model, declaring that "like the English, we shall rule this empire with a handful of men.".

But the extent to which Nazism was shaped by the age of empire and whether the two systems of violence can even be compared remains the subject of intense debate.

According to recent reports, this is particularly true in Germany, where the fear is often expressed that any comparison risks relativizing or minimizing Nazi crimes, and particularly the Holocaust. Others have argued that the intense focus on the Nazi era has, at least in part, come at the expense of a meaningful reckoning with Germany's colonial history.

"I do think this is nonsense," states Stephan Malinowski, a Professor of Modern European History at the University of Edinburgh. "If it were true, then all other colonial countries who are not discussing the Holocaust, like Great Britain for example, or France or Spain or Portugal, they would then supposedly be very, very attentive to colonial crimes and to colonial history, which it seems to me is not the case.".

"Controversial Kinship: Colonial and National Socialist Violence," a latest exhibition at the German Historical Museum in Berlin curated by Malinowski, does not aim to settle the debate but to tell its story.

It has been revealed that the exhibition begins with a hippopotamus-hide whip used in African colonies displayed alongside a canister of Zyklon B, the poison used in Nazi gas chambers. The juxtaposition highlights the contrast between colonial violence and the industrialized mass murder of the Holocaust. Yet it also points to connections: Whips were used in Nazi concentration camps, while Fascist Italy deployed chemical weapons against civilians and soldiers during its invasion of Ethiopia (then Abyssinia) in 1935-36.

Sources indicate that in the 1930s, anti-colonial thinkers from India to the Caribbean argued that colonialism and fascism were two sides of the same coin. "There is nothing new or original about the blustering exploits of Hitler and Mussolini," observed the Trinidadian journalist and Pan-Africanist George Padmore in 1938. "They have all been used before by the British in their efforts to obtain the subjection of less powerfully armed and more industrially backward people.".

European colonial rule was marked by the ruthless exploitation of people and resources, often enforced through extreme violence. In "The Origins of Totalitarianism" (1951), German-American philosopher Hannah Arendt argued that colonial territories served as laboratories for racial ideologies and practices of domination that could be applied beyond the legal constraints of Europe. Arendt described how these later "boomeranged" back into Europe and helped shape totalitarian politics in distinct and unprecedented form.

The Congo Free State, King Leopold II of Belgium's private colony from 1885 to 1908, became notorious for its extreme brutality, as colonial authorities used executions, amputations and sexual violence to ensure rubber production quotas were met. Forced labor was also central to Nazi rule, with millions of Poles, Ukrainians, Russians and others from the Soviet Union, and Jews, subjected to exploitation and "Vernichtung durch Arbeit" ("extermination through work"). Within a few years, the regime mobilized around 13 to 14 million forced laborers, a scale comparable to the transatlantic slave trade over more than three centuries. The Nazis sought to extract value from their victims at every stage, confiscating their property, exploiting their labor, and even harvesting gold teeth and hair from the dead.

Industry observers note that while racism underpinned both colonial empires and Nazism, Malinowski says the goals were different. The colonial powers tended to present assimilation as a path to advancement, forcing colonized people to adopt European culture, serve imperial interests, and suggesting that a select, educated few could gain opportunities at elite institutions such as Oxford or Cambridge. "This is definitely not something that the Nazi regime is offering to Poles or to Russians or let alone to Jews," added Malinowski.

"In terms of violence, colonial violence was just as extreme as Nazi violence. But Nazi violence was annihilatory and exterminatory compared to colonial violence in the colonies," says Edward Kissi, a historian at the School of Interdisciplinary Global Studies at the University of South Florida. He points to the example of how, unlike European colonial powers in Africa, the Nazis pursued the elimination of Black-Germans or peoples of African descent in Germany through forced sterilization. "Even in racism, colonial color-based racism and colonial anti-Jewish sentiments were fundamentally different from what the Nazis pursued.".

On October 2, 1904, German General Lothar von Trotha issued the "Vernichtungsbefehl" ("extermination order") following the Herero uprising in German South West Africa (present-day Namibia). Historians generally attribute the order to a combination of racial ideology, a desire to terrorize the population into submission, and efforts to secure colonial control over land, labor and resources. Between 1904 and 1908, an estimated 60,000 to 80,000 Herero (around 80% of the population) and 10,000 (around half the population) Nama died.

Sources indicate that one area where the exhibition draws no direct parallel is the industrialized killing carried out in Nazi death camps such as Belzec, Sobibor, Treblinka, and Auschwitz-Birkenau. "Where the two things really diverge is the Holocaust and is the systematic mass murder of the European Jews and it's murder for the very purpose of murder," explains Malinowski. The deportation of around 1,800 Jews from the Greek islands of Rhodes and Kos in July 1944 illustrates how Nazi persecution often defied military or economic logic. Even after the war was effectively lost, the community was transported to Auschwitz, where most were murdered immediately upon arrival.

It has been revealed that the issue of the "singularity" of the Holocaust came to the fore during the 1980s "Historikerstreit" ("historians' dispute"). Historian Ernst Nolte argued that Nazism should be understood in the wider context of 20th-century political violence, and as a response to Bolshevik terror in particular. Critics accused him of downplaying German responsibility for Nazi crimes.

Since 2020, a renewed debate dubbed the "Historikerstreit 2.0" has focused on whether the Holocaust should be viewed as a unique reference point in German memory culture or be understood alongside the histories of colonialism, racism and empire. The dispute now is less about the legitimacy of comparison than about its implications.

The mass murder of tens of thousands of the Herero and Nama during four years of German colonial rule is now regarded as the first genocide of the 20th-century. In 2016, Nama representatives walked out of talks after Germany's chief negotiator remarked what happened was "incomparable" to the Holocaust. The German government has since recognized the events as genocide "from today's perspective," but it has not yet accepted legal liability or agreed to pay formal reparations.

Martinican intellectual Aime Cesaire argued in "Discourse on Colonialism" (1950) that Europe condemned under Nazism forms of violence it had long accepted in its colonies. The exhibition opens amid renewed debates over settler colonialism, the definition of genocide, and the meaning of "never again," sharpened by Nicaragua's case against Germany at the International Court of Justice over German support for Israel during the war in Gaza. These tensions are reflected in visitors' comments in the exhibition's epilogue, even though the exhibition itself does not address Israel or Palestine beyond a reference to Mohammed Amin al-Husseini, appointed Grand Mufti of Jerusalem in 1921.

Industry observers note that germany has unequivocally accepted responsibility for the Holocaust, which is front and center of the country's culture of remembrance. However, Kissi likens Germany's apparent reluctance to reckon with its colonial history to debates in the US over slavery, in Cambodia over the Khmer Rouge, and in Turkey over the Armenian genocide. According to him, Germany's contemporary identity cannot be fully understood without examining its colonial history and the ways the Nazis appropriated and transformed aspects of that legacy. "I think Germans and all other human beings who have experienced violent pasts and difficult pasts should be very careful not to delink or dissociate those facts from their present," Kissi stated. "These are historical patterns. It is better to deal with these historical patterns and discomforts than to just fight them and then say this has absolutely nothing to do with German national identity.".

"Controversial Kinship: Colonial and National Socialist Violence" is on show at the German Historical Museum until April 11, 2027.

Premier League presenter Ellie Collins issued a warning to her followers after learning that she had been being impersonated on social media.

The 26-year-old has over 58,000 followers on Instagram having built up a loyal fanbase via her work on broadcasters covering the top flight and NFL in the US.

But Collins was forced to make a statement after an imposter was found to have been reaching out to people in her name over a number of months.

'I want to make people aware that someone has been impersonating me on WhatsApp, messaging high-profile athletes, pretending to be me with their username set to my name and a picture of me,' she told her followers on the social media app.

'This has been happening on and off for several months and seems to be upping in frequency more recently.

'I have reported this to the police and they’ve asked that I share it on here to make people aware, particularly anyone I have worked with or connected with in the football/sports world.

Premier League presenter Ellie Collins has warned fans of an impersonator pretending to be her on social media (All photos source: Instagram/Ellie Collins).

The 26-year-old maintains an active presence on the site and has over 58,000 followers.

After previously working as a waitress, Collins transitioned into broadcasting four years ago.

Since starting her career in the media, Collins has had the opportunity to interview a number of sports stars including Frank Lampard.

'If you receive a message from someone claiming to be me... it’s most likely not. If you don’t have my personal number and are unsure, just DM me on Instagram.

'If you receive anything suspicious, please send it to me directly so I can keep a record of it.

'Thank youuu (purple heart emoji, winking emoji),' she signed off.

Collins has worked in the media since joining IMG Media as an assistant five years ago.

Since 2022, the former waitress has served as a presenter for Premier League productions, which has led to opportunities to interview sports stars including Andy Robertson, John Terry, Bruno Fernandes, Conor Gallagher and Cody Gakpo.

Collins has also worked a number of events beyond the domestic league, such as Wimbledon and the 2025 Champions League final.

This year, she also covered the Open for Sky Sports from Royal Birkdale, and racing at York's Ebor Festival with ITV.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 09:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:00.

England should be seen as the favourites to win the UEFA Nations League ahead of the quarter-final draw, a former Three Lions striker has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Thomas Tuchel's side will learn their knockout fate on Friday morning when the draw for the last eight is held, and England head into the ceremony as one of the four seeded teams courtesy of finishing first in League A Group 3.

The Three Lions unexpectedly pipped world and European champions Spain to top spot courtesy of an engrossing 3-2 win over La Roja on Sunday, ending an unparalleled 43-game unbeaten run for Luis de la Fuente's side.

England will meet one of Belgium, Netherlands or Norway in the quarter-finals, while France, Portugal and Germany represent the other three Group A winners going for glory.

Despite the strength of the draw, former England striker Mark Hateley believes that Tuchel's men have made themselves the favourites to win the trophy for the first time, and also reserved special praise foe the goalkeeping heroics of James Trafford.

In a recent development, asked if England are leading the charge for Nations League stardom, Hateley replied: "100%. That's the best I've seen England, or any team, play over a period of, say, 60 minutes.

"They were incredible: high press, press, press, press, going man for man, confident enough to go man for man at the back against the world champions, allowing your midfield players to jump up with the strikers.

Sources indicate that “It was tremendous to watch, the very best we've seen from an England side for many, many years, honestly. It was superb. We went to 3-0, rightly so, and Spain never had a shot. Their first was 50 minutes in, in the second half.

It has been revealed that “Trafford must have thought 'this was a goddamn easy game.' The only time I think he was at fault was his starting position for the penalty, when Anderson brought the boy down. If his starting position had been higher, I think he'd have made the interception. That would be my only fault for the goalkeeper.

“If you’re a shot stopper, you’re a shot stopper - it’s just the other side of his game, where you're reading it and where you should be, playing as that sweeper.

"With the way we were pressing, the only ball really on for Spain was a ball in behind into the last third, which was empty for long periods. There was nobody there where I thought he could have been. But those are the things you pick up on and learn from.”.

England have only ever competed in the Nations League knockout stages once before in the inaugural 2018-19 edition, when they reached the finals courtesy of beating Spain and Croatia to first place in their group.

However, at a time when the Nations League Finals only comprised four teams, Gareth Southgate's side fell to a 3-1 loss to the Netherlands in the semi-finals, meaning that they are still awaiting their first knockout-phase win in the tournament.

England could only place third in the group stage of the 2020-21 tournament, before an embarrassing relegation to League B in the 2022-23 edition, although they swiftly returned to the top tier.

In the current format, England's record of five wins, one loss and 19 goals scored represented their best-ever performance in the group stage of the Nations League, fuelling the belief that the Three Lions can finally end their trophy drought in 2027.

Mark Hateley was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of London.bet.
