Premier League football will soon resume after the international break, with Manchester City hoping to rectify their recent troubles against Fulham in Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

Since suffering their first loss of the Premier League season to Aston Villa, City have fallen to two further defeats at the hands of Brighton and Nottingham Forest.

With time to think over the international break, Enzo Maresca has decisions to make when it comes to his starting XI for the visit of Fulham to the Etihad this weekend.

In a recent development, he has headaches in defence. Marc Guehi missed international duty with England after coming off with an matter against Nottingham Forest, while he has since confirmed Abdukodir Khusanov and Matheus Nunes are both doubts for the match, too. Antoine Semenyo is a long-term absentee with a knee issue.

In goal, Gianluigi Donnarumma has come under fire for his performances, but it seems unlikely that Maresca would drop the Italian international just yet.

With Guehi and Khusanov doubts, it makes sense to predict a centre-back pairing of Ruben Dias and Josko Gvardiol. Left back Nico O’Reilly is returning to both form and favour with Maresca, while Nunes may be forced to drop out for Rico Lewis.

Enzo Fernandez is definitely a favourite of Maresca, and while the Argentine travelled to South America to play two friendlies with his national side, he was rested for 35 minutes in the second game.

Elliott Anderson received a similar amount of rest while away with England - coming off early during their 3-2 victory over Spain courtesy of a red card.

City paid over £250million to overhaul their midfield this summer, and the duo’s quality should see them start.

In a recent development, phil Foden was dropped for the defeat to Forest, but City’s performance might encourage Maresca to restore the England international to the starting XI. In order to fit both Foden and Rayan Cherki into the side, the former will have to go on the right wing, with the latter playing centrally.

We’re predicting that Jeremy Doku will get the nod on the left - with Erling Haaland leading the line up top.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 10:00.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has revealed that Bukayo Saka will spend another four weeks on the sidelines with the quadriceps injury he sustained against Bayern Munich in the Champions League.

Saka's injury occurred in the first half of Arsenal's 2-2 draw with the Bundesliga champions on October 21, and Arteta immediately conceded at full time that the winger's problem looked severe.

Reports emerging soon after stated that Saka would miss between six and eight weeks, although Arsenal have been loath to put an exact timeframe on the Englishman's recovery just yet.

However, speaking to the media ahead of Saturday's Premier League clash with Newcastle United, Arteta admitted that Saka was only halfway into his recovery process and would spend the full eight weeks out.

Recent findings suggest that "We had another test. It looks like it’s going to be an eight week injury more or less. He’s four weeks in now," the Spaniard told reporters.

Saka missing another four weeks means that the 25-year-old is set to sit out another seven matches across all competitions, including a number of heavyweight fixtures.

Arsenal host Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League next Tuesday, before ending the month with a clash of the titans against Manchester City in the Premier League.

Saka is also expected to miss matches with Brentford, Tottenham Hotspur and Real Madrid in early December, and he will most likely be unavailable for the visit of Bournemouth on December 13 too.

However, the attacker could be fit to make his comeback against Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United on December 20, until when Noni Madueke and Max Dowman will provide cover.

Dowman will serve the third of his three-game domestic suspension against Newcastle this weekend, but Madueke has earned numerous plaudits in recent weeks, having scored against Slavia Prague in the Champions League before firing the effort that led to Martin Odegaard's winner against Hull City.

Saka will likely be one of two core members of Arsenal's title-winning team to miss matches against Tottenham and Real Madrid, as Arteta also delivered negative news on Martin Zubimendi.

The midfielder appeared to hurt his hamstring in Spain's 3-2 Nations League defeat to England during the international break, and he also faces around a month on the sidelines.

Industry observers note that "He has a problem in his hamstring. The scan highlights there is an injury there he will be out for a few weeks," Arteta added on Zubimendi.

However, the 27-year-old is yet to start a Premier League game this season and was always expected to lose out to Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes at St James' Park tomorrow.

Arsenal are five points clear at the top of the Premier League table heading into gameweek 11 and are searching for their fourth successive win over Newcastle in the top flight.

The second international break of the season is upon us, which is a good time to take stock of how things are going beyond he men’s first team.

Industry observers note that an ownership and management should not just be judged on one area of the club, but rather multiple different departments. The youth sector needs to be developing players in the right way, while the rising prevalence of women’s football gives added impetus to make the Femminile side as competitive as possible.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

That being remarked, can be hard enough keeping up with how the senior team are doing without thinking about the various other sides operating under the Milan umbrella. So, we have provided a summary of how Milan Futuro, Milan Primavera and Milan Women are doing so far in 2026-27.

It was all change over the summer for the Futuro as they brought in Sergio Navarro as the head coach. The idea was to create some continuity with Ruben Amorim’s more continental style of football, and the pedigree that the Spaniard has suggested it was a positive move.

While not a necessity, the objective for the campaign will no doubt have been set as competing for promotion back to the third tier, which is the level that the project started at prior to the relegation in 2024-25.

Position: It is a case of so far, so good for Navarro’s men. They sit fourth in the standings with 23 points from 11 games, obtained through seven wins, two draws and two losses. They have scored 21 goals (third-most in the league) and allowed 15.

Importantly, the Futuro have a game in hand on the sides above them. If they win it they would go level with Chievo Verona (yes, that Chievo) and Nibbiano & Valtidone who are on 26 points. The former, however, have a 10 better goal difference.

The U23s are part of the Premier League International Cup and they got past Everton 2-1 in the first game, with matches against Stoke later this month and Tottenham in November to come, both away from home.

High point: On October 18, Milan’s second team went to the current league-leaders Chievo and beat them 2-1, with Bonomi scoring a late winner. That was an early marker of what this team are capable of. A special mention must go to the Premier League Cup win at Goodison Park against Everton, too.

Low point: That aforementioned win in Verona came in the round after Milan had lost 2-1 at home to Rovato Vertovese. They are a side that have only won twice all season and right now occupy the relegation spots, so it was a massive blow before a big response.

In a recent development, key players: There have been multiple players that have stood out. Levin Asanji has scored four goals in the league, as has Lorenzo Ossolo. Fabio Pandolfi has been playing a deeper midfield role and looks to have quality well beyond his 18 years of age, with three goals to his name.

Recent findings suggest that silvano Vos is having a resurgence, while the likes of Emanuele Sala, Mattia Cappelletti, Alessandro Bonomi and Emanuele Borsani have all started every single game, aiding their development under the latest coach. El Hadji Malick Cisse – a January arrival – is also turning a lot of heads.

For a bit more deeper reading on the tactical approach used by Milan Futuro under Navarro, we suggest reading the analysis we put out over the international break.

The 2025-26 season was a mixed one for the Primavera side, as their record of 11 wins and 11 defeats in 38 games highlights perfectly. They finished 11th, nine points off the relegation play-offs but 10 points off the Scudetto play-offs, though a lot of the younger talents had been again accelerated into the Futuro side.

Recent findings suggest that giovanni Renna remained at the helm going into the new campaign, the coach that has been promoted up the ranks and thus knows a lot of the players. The hope was that continuity would yield better results, and so far it has.

Position: At the time of writing, the U20 side are sixth in the Primavera 1 league, which puts them in a final play-off spot. They have won five of their first 10 games but they have also lost four, so they remain a bit of a rollercoaster ride of inconsistency.

It has been revealed that looking upwards, Parma are right now top on 21 points, but the Rossoneri are within striking distance of Inter, who are in second on 19 points. However, Renna’s side are also a bad round away from being in the bottom half too.

Recent findings suggest that milan Primavera progressed in the Coppa Italia Primavera at the end of October, beating Catanzaro 2-1 thanks to a late winner from Dotta. Como are the opponents in the next round.

Sources indicate that high point: It’s hard to look past the last two rounds in truth. The Primavera seem to have really clicked, scoring 10 goals in the last 180 minutes of action, beating Monza 5-0 away from home and then AlbinoLeffe 5-1 at home.

An honourable mention must go to the 2-0 win over Juventus in September, given they are in a similar position with also having a B-team (Juve Next Gen), so they will continue to serve as a useful point of comparison.

Low point: Back on October 10, the young Diavoli lost 2-0 against Atalanta which was their third league defeat in a row. There was talk of crisis mode as the slide down the table continued, and against an Atalanta side that are now third-bottom of the league. Thankfully, they turned it around quickly.

Industry observers note that key players: A bit like with the Futuro, the goals have been shared around the Milan Primavera squad. Mattia Zaramella has emerged recently as a star with four goals, as has Max Anastasio who arrived from Bologna and has the same amount.

According to recent reports, then, Andrea Cullotta (a centre-back), Vincent Ibrahimovic (a midfielder) and Edoardo Tartaglia (a full-back) all have two goals. Renna has called upon the same core group of players largely. Matteo Geroli, Francesco Domnitei, Cullotta, Zaramella, Tartaglia, Anastasio and Yanis Massaouadi have all appeared in every round.

Last season was not one that Milan Women will want to shout about, given that they finished sixth in the table and seven points off the play-off spots in the end. They won just nine of 22 games, placing them below even Fiorentina and Lazio, plus Juventus, city rivals Inter and eventual champions Roma.

However, like with the Primavera, consistency was the name of the game. So, Suzanne Bakker remained as the head coach, and there wasn’t as much player turnover as in some recent years.

Position: There have only been seven rounds so far in Serie A Femminile, but the Rossonere have got off to a stuttering start. They have just seven points from their opening seven games, which puts them in eighth place in the table. They have scored 11 goals but let in a joint-league-high 16.

It has been revealed that looking upwards, Roma lead the way with 21 points having won every game. Inter are second on 16 points – so nine more than Milan – while Juventus occupy the final play-off spot on 12. Over their shoulders, Sassuolo are in bottom (the only relegation spot), with three points.

In the Women’s Cup, Milan drew 1-1 with Como, beat Como 1907 (affiliated with the men’s team currently in Serie A, the others are a stand-alone club) 2-1, and then lost 1-0 to Juventus to end their campaign.

It has been revealed that high point: This one is quite an easy pick, and it has to be the 2-1 victory over Juventus last month. Thea Kyvåg and Monica Renzotti overturned Lenzini’s opener, which had come with just under a quarter of an hour left on the clock, engineering a late comeback that sparked jubilant scenes.

Low point: The tone for what has been a disappointing campaign so far for Bakker’s ladies was set in round one, when they were beaten 4-1 by Como 1907. Then, losing 1-0 away at Como was another dark day, given they have only won twice.

On November 7, the 3-0 derby defeat to Inter – which included a red card for Milan – served only to highlight the big gulf between the two teams at the moment.

Recent findings suggest that key players: Christy Grimshaw remains the shining light for Milan Women, with three goals and an assist to her name. The scoring charts then see Sara Stokic on three goals, with Sara Fornes, Park Soojeong and Monica Renzotti all netting twice.

Grimshaw is one of three players to start every game so far under Bakker, with the others being defenders Angelica Soffia and Nerea Nevado. Sandra Estevez has emerged as the number one between the sticks too.

#14306. Latest Update: DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's crucial.

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (947 w)
📖 Baca

Latest Update: DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's crucial.

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (947 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that you know when you lock your phone and the screen goes black?
  • Imagine you're sitting on a bus, staring out of a window, taking a shower or walking, and you get that feeling of doing nothing and letting your mind drift?
  • Well, your mind, the brain, is doing a lot when it feels like you're doing nothing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that you know when you lock your phone and the screen goes black? It seems like it's not doing anything. But it's not doing nothing. It's syncing your messages, updating apps and running other background processes.

Your brain has its own version of that.

Imagine you're sitting on a bus, staring out of a window, taking a shower or walking, and you get that feeling of doing nothing and letting your mind drift?

Well, your mind, the brain, is doing a lot when it feels like you're doing nothing.

It's going over your memories, shaping your sense of who you are, imagining possible futures, helping you understand other people and connecting ideas.

That's your brain's default mode network.

Scientists conducted brain-imaging experiments in the 1990s and early 2000s to find out which regions of the brain were active during demanding tasks, like solving a math problem or memory exercise.

It has been revealed that but to measure that, they needed a so-called baseline. They needed to know the level of brain activity at rest and during demanding tasks.

So, between the tasks, they asked participants to relax, close their eyes, stare at a fixed point on a wall, or try not to think of anything at all.

It has been revealed that and they measured the participants' brain activity both when they were solving a task and doing nothing. That's how scientists noticed the brain was active in up- and downtime.

They noticed that when participants started to focus on a upcoming task, after having done nothing, some brain areas lit up and other areas dimmed down. That suggests those areas that dimmed down must have been active while the participant was apparently — physically and mentally — at rest.

This realization eventually led to the discovery of the default mode network or DMN.

The DMN is crucial because it helps your brain make sense of your life and experiences.

It helps you connect and revisit memories, reflect on who you are, imagine what might happen in future scenarios, understand other people, build meaning from experience, and connect ideas in new ways.

It turns all your memories, experiences, knowledge, emotions and social information into your internal story. Think of that story as a constantly evolving, updated model of who you are and how you engage with the world around you.

But it's important to understand the DMN involves more than one area of the brain. It is a group of brain regions that light up when you're not focused on an external task.

Recent findings suggest that there's another player in your brain that acts as a monitoring system. You can think of it as constantly asking "Is there anything that needs my attention?".

Imagine you're daydreaming while driving, and a car suddenly swerves into your lane.

Recent findings suggest that in a fraction of a second, your daydream disappears and your attention snaps back to the road. That player is called the salience network, or SN.

The salience network helps you notice crucial signals, like a sound, a mistake, pain, an emotion, a threat, or something happening in your body, and helps shift the brain toward attention and control systems when action is needed.

The DMN, SN and attention/control systems constantly interact.

Sources indicate that and the DMN doesn't just turn off completely with every hard task. Parts of it can also contribute when tasks involve memory, stories, meaning or other people.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Smartphones have filled many of the small empty moments of our days — waiting for the bus, standing in line, eating alone, lying on the couch. We are constantly looking at our devices.

So, it seems reasonable to ask: are we crowding out those moments of boredom where DMN kicks in?

According to recent reports, maybe. But so far, there's no strong evidence that scrolling directly affects mental health by reducing DMN time.

What we do know is that problematic smartphone use can increase stress, anxiety, task-switching and disrupt sleep.

And sleep loss and stress also have clearer evidence for altering DMN-related brain connectivity.

The DMN is not always necessarily good.

When your mind wanders, it might produce a great new idea.

According to recent reports, but it might also replay an embarrassing thing you did five years ago. Again. And again.

In depression, the self-reflection part of the DMN can get caught in repetitive negative loops that are hard to stop — what's known as rumination.

Scientists have also found that Alzheimer's disease targets key DMN areas, particularly those responsible for your autobiographical memory and remembering other aspects of the past. Which may help explain why memory problems are so central to the disease.

Protect your sleep and take stress seriously. There is direct evidence that sleep loss and stress disrupt DMN-related connectivity.

Take real, quiet breaks after mentally demanding tasks, like studying. It can even help you memorize facts for your exam.

Embrace boredom and enjoy doing nothing.

Try to reframe boredom as this essential, energy-intensive active work in your brain that builds your internal narrative and sense of self, consolidates memories, creates connections and sparks creativity.

Industry observers note that try waiting in line without checking your phone. Look out the window next time you take the bus or take a walk without listening to anything.

Recent findings suggest that you can also try scheduling DMN time. It may be the closest thing to a real brain hack.

Mauricio Pochettino will pick his first Manchester United team on Sunday for a daunting debut away at Liverpool.

The Argentine was appointed Michael Carrick’s successor last week and only arrived in the north-west on Wednesday, leaving him just a handful of sessions to prepare his side for a crunch fixture.

As such, wholesale changes from life under Carrick are not forecast, at least in terms of setup. After all, both managers have a penchant for the same 4-2-3-1 formation.

Carlos Baleba remains sidelined with a hamstring injury sustained against Roma in the Champions League, with Benjamin Sesko also out until the newly introduced year, but Pochettino may well be boosted by the returns of Marcus Rashford and Luke Shaw. The latter seems the more likely of the two, with Rashford yet to be pictured in training since the international break.

Pochettino is known to be very fond of Rashford, and has reportedly attempted to sign him to other teams he has managed, meaning he can expect to get the nod if fit.

Sources indicate that should fit-again Shaw slot in at left-back, he may do so as one of two fresh faces in the back four. Lisandro Martinez has served his red card suspension and will be available to partner Harry Maguire, with Diogo Dalot at right-back.

A midfield pairing of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo will sit behind the trio of Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Amad Diallo, with Bryan Mbeumo leading the line.

Patrick Dorgu is expected to be fit, too, but it remains to be seen whether he can unseat Matheus Cunha off the left. He could also deputise Shaw if his fitness levels are not up to par.

Sources indicate that leaked drone footage of United’s Thursday training session appeared to show Pochettino working on tactics with a tight-knit group of ten outfield players, leading some to speculate that he might be dealing with Sunday’s starters. The presence of Joshua Zirkzee and Harry Amass in the group rather debunks this, though, given neither has started a Premier League match this season.

Predicted Man Utd XI vs Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw; Tielemans, Mainoo; Amad, Fernandes, Cunha; Mbeumo.

Time and date: 4.30pm GMT on Sunday, November 22.

Jose Mourinho has once again called Vinicius Junior "an incredible player" following a positive international break for the Real Madrid winger.

Vinicius has struggled for Los Blancos this season, scoring just once and providing three assists in 12 appearances across all competitions.

The 26-year-old also missed Madrid's last four LaLiga matches before the break after receiving a straight red card for a hair pull against Villarreal.

However, during the international break with Brazil, Vinicius scored a brace against Japan before netting a hat-trick against Singapore.

Ahead of Madrid's league meeting with Celta Vigo, Mourinho reiterated his support for Vinicius.

"Starter, off the bench, or in the stands, it doesn't matter," Mourinho said about Vinicius' role in the team.

"It's a strange thing because, a couple of weeks ago, people were talking about Vinicius as if he were the huge problem Real Madrid had, and after scoring goals against Singapore and Japan, we can't stop talking about Vinicius: if he plays, if he doesn't, why he has to play.

"I think it's too much. What I say about Vinicius is what I've said one, two, three, four, and five weeks ago: he is an incredible player, we love him, we need him, we have always tried to help him, and that's what we will continue to do.

"Here, we don't have players with privileges. We don't have players who have to play by decree. We have a group of people working for the team, for Real Madrid.".

In a recent development, "Celta are much better than the points they have," said Mourinho. They are a team that last season beat us here, at the Bernabeu.

"They are playing in Europe, and perhaps playing matches on Thursdays and then in the league is also costing them some points, but this factor does not exist [for this fixture].

"They will surely present themselves as always: organised and ambitious. They concede few goals because, defensively, they are very organised, and they know how to do it and how to press.".

Kylian Mbappe has scored in each of his last seven appearances for Madrid in all competitions (nine goals) and could equal his best scoring run for the club, achieved between September and October 2025 (eight games, 12 goals).

Williot Swedberg has scored more LaLiga goals against Madrid than against any other side (four in five games).

Since the start of 2024-25, he has been involved in five league goals against Madrid (four goals, one assist), the joint-most alongside Raphinha.

MATCH PREDICTION – REAL MADRID WIN.

Madrid have lost just one of their last 24 LaLiga games against Celta (W21 D2), a 2-0 defeat in December 2025, winning 11 of the last 12.

Los Blancos have won their last eight games in all competitions, their best winning run since a 10-game streak between May and September 2022 under Carlo Ancelotti.

However, Madrid lost their last home game against Celta in LaLiga and have only twice lost consecutive home games against them in the competition (L2 in 1943 and in 2006).

Celta have picked up points in six of their last seven away games against teams from the Community of Madrid in LaLiga (W3 D3 L1), but they lost their most recent such match 3-0 against Rayo Vallecano last October.

Celta have conceded 10 goals and kept six clean sheets in LaLiga 2026-27, both their best records after the first 12 games of a season in the competition since 2002-03 (eight goals and seven clean sheets), under Miguel Angel Lotina.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There will be many more Champions League nights for Rio Ngumoha, although the 18-year-old will always remember this career landmark when his teenage skill plunged the opposition into fearful indecision and decided the game.

Sources indicate that this young man has not yet played 40 senior games but there is no doubting the quality. Alexis Mac Allister scored twice, Liverpool came from two goals behind, and it all ended with a panic that meant they came close to chucking it away again. But what everyone could agree on from this strange match of fluctuating fortunes was that Ngumoha looks like one of the best young players in Europe. He is also a bona fide two-sided winger, winning this game for Liverpool from the right wing rather than his conventional left-wing role.

It has been revealed that ngumoha created the second Liverpool goal for Ronald Araújo and then the third for Mac Allister with the game’s best moment. That was an electrifying run into a group of converging yellow shirts in which he beat two men and still retained the composure to pick out Mac Allister in the area. Even as the Argentine ran to the Kop to celebrate, that stand was chanting the name of the teenager from east London. Ngumoha was one of three academy boys in Andoni Iraola’s XI, along with Lewis Koumas and Trey Nyoni, and all had an impact.

Magic from Rio Ngumoha 🤩🪄 Alexis Mac Allister puts Liverpool ahead with his second goal of the night ⚽️ https://t.co/3FTNWOUYhl.

The one Crystal Palace tradition that Thomas Frank must change if former Tottenham boss is to succeed

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, crystal Palace sacked Pierre Sage and hired Thomas Frank because they needed change. They need more than their latest manager seems to realise.

The Dane revealed on Thursday that the 3-4-3 formation Palace have become so used to playing under Oliver Glasner and then briefly under Sage will “definitely be one of our systems, a go-to - and then we'll see what we change.”.

The truth, though, is that while flexibility is good, the formation is one of the things that does need a rethink.

Frank was right about one thing, at least. “It is obvious that this squad is recruited to 3-4-3”, he noted. “That's why we have very good players in their positions.”.

It has been revealed that but those “very good players” are not still at Selhurst Park. The Eagles have been persevering with a system that suits players no longer at the club, something the new boss must put right.

Wind the clock back less than a year and after a 2-1 win over London rivals Fulham, Palace sat fourth in the Premier League table in a season destined produce historic European silverware.

Instead, a 29-minute capitulation that resulted in a 5-4 defeat in South Wales has left relegation feeling increasingly likely, even though the season is only just under a third of the way complete.

Burnley remain on 10 points from 15 matches, their only success coming at fellow strugglers Watford, and they are already five points adrift of safety.

Although an upturn in fortunes would see them quickly haul themselves back into contention to avoid the drop, conceding 31 goals - the worst defensive record in the Championship - will not fill supporters with confidence.

Five of Burnley's seven Championship games at Turf Moor this season have ended in draws, but they remain the only team in the division without a home victory.

As for Blackburn, they have an interim management team in place after Tony Mowbray stood down from his position earlier this week due to health issues.

Rovers sit 11 points above their fierce rivals in the standings, the pre-season expectation having been that the points difference would be close to the exact opposite at this stage of the campaign.

Nevertheless, Blackburn have won five of their last nine fixtures in the second tier to keep them in the hunt for a playoff spot.

However, Connor Roberts starts a three-game ban, a consequence of an incident at the end of the Cardiff game that led to retrospective punishment.

Despite Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds taking the reins from Mowbray, the Blackburn XI will look similar from the victory over West Ham.

However, second-choice goalkeeper Aynsley Pears is expected to deputise for Balazs Toth, who suffered a finger injury while on international duty with Hungary.

If the likes of Mathias Jorgensen and Ryoya Morishita overcome injuries in time for this fixture, they will likely be named on the substitutes' bench at best.

Weiss; Walker, Ekdal, Alleyne, Pires; Hatate, Cullen; Ramazani, Edwards, Amdouni; Hountondji.

Blackburn Rovers possible starting lineup:.

Pears; Beyuku, Carter, McLoughlin, Pickering; Morsy, Montgomery; Fevrier, Cantwell, Afolayan; Gudjohnsen.

Gary Neville has stood up for under-fire Manchester United man Diogo Dalot – and named three of his defensive team-mates he would rather see leave the club before him.

The Portugal international's limp performances have come under heavy scrutiny this season with the decline of Michael Carrick's side as autumn has worn on.

But as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to take over at Old Trafford, Neville urged the new manager not to immediately expel the defender, despite his drop-off in form.

According to recent reports, 'I think if he was in a decent back four he'd be alright,' Neville told Stick to United co-host Mark Goldbridge on Tuesday. 'But he's got a shocking back four alongside him.

'Positionally he's not great. He could be better on the ball. He could be better at everything he does. Of course he could. I just think he's such an easy target, Dalot. I honestly do.'.

Neville admitted that sometimes he listens to his fellow Man United-supporting friends deriding Dalot and wonders 'are they watching something that I don't see?'.

Gary Neville has defended Man United star Diogo Dalot - arguing that he has team-mates who are far weaker.

The Portugal international has come in for heavy criticism from supporters this season.

But in his opinion, there are three defenders that he would let go in the 'first wave' of changes in Manchester.

'I'd be getting (Noussair) Mazraoui well gone before him,' he continued. 'I'd be getting (Lisandro) Martinez gone well before him. I'll be getting (Matthijs) De Ligt gone well before him.

Recent findings suggest that '(De Ligt has) got one substantial problem. He doesn’t play football. If a player is injury prone and doesn't play football, just because he hasn't played doesn't mean to say that he should go above a player who's played every single week and he's throwing his hand up. You want someone who's actually reliable and play. De Ligt has to go. De Ligt, Martinez, Mazraoui.'.

Another stalwart in the team that Neville was keen to have a second chance under Pochettino was Luke Shaw.

'He will keep Shaw because he knows him and he'll probably get the best out of him. The problem with Luke is injuries,' he added. 'So he'll have to manage him. So he'll have to bring a left back in. But let's just say who he'll keep.

In a recent development, 'He'll keep Shaw. He'll keep (Harry) Maguire because he'll trust him and he'll think that he's basically a soldier and someone who can do a job for him.

It has been revealed that 'He'll keep (Leny) Yoro because I think he'll think "I've got something there that I can work with". (But) I think he's a little bit gangly, all over the place right now. And he looks like he's going to slip every time. He's got that sort of Bambi-on-ice (look).

'Physically what will happen is with Yoro, he'll go one way or the other. I like the fact he's been brought into the French team. It tells me sometimes you just have got to connect the dots and think, "okay, well, if they think he's good, then we must be missing something here because we're not seeing it yet, are we?".'.

Neville went on to suggest that Yoro was lacking the connection within his body that Premier League rivals such as Jeremy Jacquet are already able to harness – something Sir Alex Ferguson had identified in Rio Ferdinand when he was at West Ham.

Like Ferdinand, Neville backed Yoro to flourish as he taps into that connection and improves his strength and stability.

In a recent development, 'So Yoro he will keep: Yoro, Maguire and Shaw I think he'll keep and I think he'll keep Dalot. To start with,' Neville remarked. 'He'll have to bring in three defenders to go above them. Let's be clear. He'll have to bring in three defenders.

'Mazraoui I would lose, De Ligt I would lose because he's injury prone. Martinez 100 per cent. 100 per cent. 100 per cent.'.

As well as struggling for form this season, Martinez has been a challenging presence in the Man United squad this term, boldly calling out the Man United hierarchy during a firebrand interview last month.

Neville was more interested in new head coach Mauricio Pochettino despatching Noussair Mazraoui and Matthijs de Ligt.

Lisandro Martinez has been an unsettled presence in the side this season and hit out at the club's recruiting last month.

The Argentina star implied that he was disappointed with the club's recruitment strategy over the summer, and was forced to hold clear-the-air talks to smooth his return to the side.

Neville added that he would send Ayden Heaven on loan to get experience in the lower divisions to 'build' his ability up, as it was borderline 'unfair' to be 'putting him in' the side at present.

But not all of the changes can come rapidly for Pochettino, who has little time before taking charge of Man United against Liverpool at Anfield this weekend.

In a recent development, 'First wave, end of the season,' Neville clarified of what he believes Pochettino's strategy for change will be. 'No, he can't get rid of (them all) in January.

Industry observers note that 'He has to bring one or two defenders in January if he can. But he can't get rid of all those in his first wave. He's only got one month till January.'.

The drawn-out process of sacking Carrick began last week when Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada flew to Monaco for talks with co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer ownership group.

While his future was on the chopping block, Carrick held training sessions at Carrington before the axe finally swung last Thursday.

Pochettino was appointed days later and gave a tearful farewell press conference ahead of his penultimate game with the United States national team on Saturday.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he told the press. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

According to recent reports, ‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay. I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

It has been revealed that ‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

Recent findings suggest that ‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Real Betis boss Manuel Pellegrini revealed he "would rather go to the Champions League and not win than win the derbies and finish 15th".

Betis take on rivals Sevilla in LaLiga on Saturday, with both sides looking to make a push for the Champions League places this season.

Betis are fourth after 10 games, seven points behind leaders Barcelona following a 2-0 win over Elche before the international break.

Sevilla, meanwhile, are eight points behind their rivals in sixth ahead of their clash at Estadio Ramon Sanchez Pizjuan.

It has been revealed that pellegrini has won two of his last three LaLiga games against Sevilla (D1), after failing to win any of his previous 10 (D6 L4). Away from home, he has only won three of his 15 matches against Sevilla in the competition (D3 L9).

The former Manchester City boss acknowledged the importance of the rivalry, but has bigger goals in mind for his Betis side.

"I expect Sevilla to have a clear, very direct style of football, they play in their own half and will be a very dangerous team," mentioned Pellegrini.

According to recent reports, "The approaches are different every year because the squads are different. Rivalry is always positive as long as it stays on the pitch and not off the field. We will try again to overcome them through our style of play.

According to recent reports, "For the fans, winning all the derbies would be vital. But if I had to choose, I'd rather go to the Champions League and not win than win the derbies and finish 15th.

"The most notable thing is to get the three points. The best way to win is to maintain the same style of play we revealed against other opponents. Playing away from home doesn't change our fundamental approach.".

Recent findings suggest that now we're all ready. We're all here  https://t.co/Tuks2y8CLU.

— Real Betis Balompié (@RealBetis_en) November 20, 2026.

Lucien Agoume has regained possession 65 times in the 2026-27 LaLiga season; only Barcelona's Pedri (69) has completed more recoveries among outfield players in the competition this term.

Marc Bartra has scored three goals in eight LaLiga games this season; only Atletico Madrid's Alejandro Grimaldo (four) has scored more among all defenders in the competition this term.

Sevilla have lost two of their last three LaLiga matches against Betis (D1) after not losing any of their previous 12 against them in the competition (W7 D5).

Sevilla have also picked up points in 11 of their last 13 home LaLiga games against Betis (W9 D2 L2), although they lost the most recent meeting 2-0 in November 2025.

Betis are unbeaten in their last four away LaLiga matches (W2 D2), keeping clean sheets in their last two. They have not recorded three consecutive away clean sheets in the competition since October 2022 (W1 D2).

Sevilla have won just one of their last five LaLiga derbies against Andalusian teams (D1 L3). Betis, however, have lost only one of their last 14 derbies in the competition (W6 D7), but that defeat was against Sevilla (1-0 in October 2024).

Sevilla boss Luis Garcia has faced Pellegrini 11 times in LaLiga, more than any other coach (P11 W2 D4 L5), failing to win any of his last six meetings with him (D4 L2).

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 10:10, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 10:12.

Barcelona need to make late checks on Jules Kounde and Pau Cubarsi before their availability for Sunday's La Liga clash with Villarreal can be determined.

Kounde has been absent since the middle of October with an ankle injury, while Cubarsi suffered a hip problem when he represented Spain against England last weekend.

Both have returned to training, but no risks will be taken ahead of a busy period, so the duo could find themselves on the bench rather than in the starting side.

Dani Olmo (adductor) is also close to a return but could ultimately just miss out.

Eric Garcia and Andreas Christensen could both be in line for spots at the back, while Marc Bernal and Fermin Lopez should join Pedri in midfield.

Anthony Gordon is again expected to join Raphinha and Lamine Yamal in the front three, with head coach Hansi Flick unlikely to spring any major surprises for this match.

Barcelona remain without the services of Roony Bardghji (knee), Xavi Espart (ankle) and Rodri (hamstring).

Barcelona possible starting lineup:.

J Garcia; E Garcia, Christensen, Martin, Cancelo; Fermin, Bernal, Pedri; Yamal, Raphinha, Gordon.

Tech Report: Can global leaders put their money where their mouth is on climate?

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1328 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The slow international response to climate change has placed the world on a path to destruction, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told heads of state and government during opening statements at this year's COP31 climate conference.
  • "The ⁠brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us," he said, as world leaders gathered in the Turkish resort city of Antalya to set the tone for negotiations at the UN climate summit.
  • In a recent development, A UN reportlast month found ​the world will cross a temperature threshold countries agreed to pursue in order to prevent runaway global heating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The slow international response to climate change has placed the world on a path to destruction, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told heads of state and government during opening statements at this year's COP31 climate conference.

"The ⁠brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us," he said, as world leaders gathered in the Turkish resort city of Antalya to set the tone for negotiations at the UN climate summit.

In a recent development, A UN reportlast month found ​the world will cross a temperature threshold countries agreed to pursue in order to prevent runaway global heating. At the same time, states like Germany are slipping down the rankings for climate action, according to the annual Climate Change Performance Index published Wednesday by New Climate Institute and Germanwatch.

Nonetheless, Guterres mentioned the world has "the power to make sure the overshoot is a temporary breach.".

Negotiators from close to 200 countries are meeting in Turkey at the end of a year characterized by extreme heat waves and a glacier collapse in Nepal that triggered a flood, killing more than 1,400 people and leaving thousands more missing.

At this year's talks, national representatives are discussing climate solutions such as increasing the share of electricity in an effort to move away from fossil fuels.

On Thursday, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, one of the few heads of government from Europe's major economies attending the summit, remarked that the world's dependence on fossil fuels was at the heart of both the climate crisis and energy security challenges.

"The shift to clean energy is the only route to energy security," he stated, endorsing the conference's focus on electrification which he said would lower energy bills, create jobs and protect people from the volatility of fossil fuel markets.

Burnham promised a "newly introduced era of British leadership over the next decade," announcing the UK would put climate resilience high on the agenda during its G20 presidency next year.

The US, the world's largest historical emitter of damaging greenhouse gases, is not attending the summit — for the second year in a row after US President Donald Trump withdrew the country from the Paris Agreement in 2025.

Other nations, including big polluters like Germany, France, Italy, Canada and Japan, also opted not to send their top leaders to the talks.

On Wednesday, Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, who is hosting COP31 together with Australia, which is leading negotiations, called on developed nations to take greater responsibility on climate finance.

Financing disagreements center around who should pay for international climate action, whether funding should take the form of grants or loans and how to scale monetary support for developing nations. Many of these countries are among the most vulnerable to the climate crisis but have contributed very little to the emissions causing it.

Erdogan noted while previous conferences had resulted in different ideas around financing, they have yet to be turned into action. "We set out to make this an implementation COP," he told leaders.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen addressed remarks that developed nations are not contributing enough to climate finance, saying that the transition away from fossil fuels is in "our common interest.".

Sources indicate that "Europe is the world's largest provider of climate finance. Last year alone, we contributed more than €32 billion [about $35.5 billion] to support developing countries," she said, adding that Europe will continue to support partners worldwide in tackling climate change.

A recent Carbon Brief analysis found that public funding pledged under the Paris Agreement to help developing countries tackle climate change fell by more than 70% in 2026.

Industry observers note that most multi-year pledges from donor countries expired in 2025. Since then, the US has stepped back from international climate efforts, while several European countries have cut their aid budgets, reported Carbon Brief.

Hilda Heine, president of the Marshall Islands in the Pacific, which face an existential threat from rising sea levels, noted the response to overshoot "must be overwhelming" and rapidly reversed otherwise "the world we know is over.".

"Every fraction of a degree of warming brings more catastrophe," mentioned Heine, adding that more warming makes it more difficult to adapt to living on a hotter planet, brings greater loss and damage from worsening weather extremes and greater financial need.

She called on leaders to triple climate finance by 2035 and make it easier for Small Island Developing States to access the money.

Recent findings suggest that "We are told there is no money, but their spending on war grows; the greatest security threat we face remains underfunded. I appeal to you: Find money for life, not death. Replenish the climate funds," Heine said.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese spoke of a "solemn responsibility to this and to future generations ​to act," adding that this is the critical decade.

Australia, the world's third-largest fossil fuel exporter, has vowed to promote the views of the "Pacific family" — small Pacific nations in the region such as Tuvalu or Fiji, where pre-COP meetings were held in October.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Albanese said it was crucial that climate cooperation delivered practical results — "unlocking investment in clean energy technologies, accelerating electrification, speeding up action for our oceans, unlocking climate finance for those who need it ​most.".

As reasons to speed up electrification von der Leyen pointed to wildfires in Europe and floods in Nepal, as well as droughts stretching from Central America to Sudan, and to the disruption to energy supplies linked to the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

"The world is witnessing the cost of continuing with the status quo for our climate and our energy security," she remarked, adding that the European Union would double down on efforts to become climate neutral.

"Three-quarters ​of humanity live in countries that import fossil fuels, hostage to price shocks they did ​not create and cannot ‌control," UN Secretary-General Guterres remarked, adding that recent conflicts have made clear a shift to renewable energy would help improve energy security and the cost-of-living crisis.

In a recent development, von der Leyen also expressed support for COP31's 35-by-35 electrification pledge. The pledge aims to increase electricity's share of final global energy use to 35% by 2035, with von der Leyen saying Europe would be the first "electro-powered" continent.

Heine of the Marshall Islands mentioned electrification must must be strictly tied to renewable energy generation rather than fossil fuels, warning that continued oil, coal and gas extraction was a threat to her country's survival.

Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said his country wanted compensation for environmental damage caused by US and Israeli strikes, including oil leaks from attacks on tankers. The strikes began in February.

Iran, which is a major fossil fuel producer and has pushed back against strict language on phasing out oil and gas at previous COPs alongside other petrostates, has also struck tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.

Pezeshkian linked the issue to climate finance and said his country expected "responsibility in times of war, to document and assess the environmental damages caused by military aggressions and to develop compensation mechanisms.".

Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who hosted last year's COP in the Amazonian city of Belem, said the momentum for climate action had dropped off at the start of the year, partly due to the Iran war.

"We started talking more about weapons and tariffs than the survival ‌of future generations," he mentioned.

He also warned that "climate agreements are the favorite targets of reactionary forces at COPs," and urged leaders to work together. Lula promised to protect the Amazon rainforest. "Brazil is back to defend the continuity of a healthy planet," he remarked.

This article was last updated on November 12 to reflect incoming statements from world leaders.

#14290. Quantum resistance paradox of low-dimensional superfluids

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 50m • 📚 Deep Dive (9975 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Quantum resistance paradox of low-dimensional superfluids

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 50 min read (9975 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~50 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, resistance in standard conductors decreases with increasing cross-section.
  • The Landau model provides a powerful framework for understanding many phases of matter through the lens of spontaneous symmetry breaking6,7.
  • For example, in a voltage-biased superconducting wire, the applied voltage continuously winds the superconducting phase, causing an increase of the phase gradient between the contacts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, resistance in standard conductors decreases with increasing cross-section. Yet, in low-dimensional superconductors and superfluids, residual resistance arises from topological fluctuations of the order parameter, manifesting as phase slips in one-dimensional (1D) and vortices in two-dimensional (2D) systems. How resistance and dissipation evolve as geometry interpolates between these regimes remains an open question. This evolution is masked in solid-state experiments by disorder, impurities and geometric imperfections1,2,3, and poses theoretical challenges due to competing dissipative processes and pronounced finite-size effects. Here, we use a defect-free unitary Fermi gas in a digitally programmable transport geometry to isolate geometric effects on superfluid dissipation and discover a paradox: in the crossover from one dimension to two dimensions, the resistance reaches a minimum. There, widening a channel increases its resistance. Narrower, quasi-1D channels show dissipation described by Langer–Ambegaokar–McCumber–Halperin theory of phase slips4. In this regime, varying the channel width yields the predicted exponential scaling of the activation factor over many orders of magnitude. Wider, quasi-2D channels show dissipation consistent with phase-slip events described by a finite-size vortex model5. The minimal dissipation in the dimensional crossover reflects a transition in the dominant dissipative mechanism, with both 1D and 2D events simultaneously suppressed. Our measurements suggest a route to minimizing dissipation in superconducting devices and provide a benchmark for theoretical efforts aimed at describing the dimensional crossover.

The Landau model provides a powerful framework for understanding many phases of matter through the lens of spontaneous symmetry breaking6,7. In superfluids and superconductors, this breaking manifests in the emergence of a macroscopic condensate that exhibits long-range phase coherence. This coherence is ultimately responsible for properties such as dissipationless transport8,9, the Josephson effect10, and in the case of superconductivity the Meissner effect11. Although relatively robust in bulk systems, in lower-dimensional systems, the enhanced effect of fluctuations—and in particular topological defects—can suppress this long-range phase coherence and govern superfluid transport4,12.

For example, in a voltage-biased superconducting wire, the applied voltage continuously winds the superconducting phase, causing an increase of the phase gradient between the contacts. The supercurrent, proportional to this gradient, would grow without bound unless intermittent phase fluctuations relax the accumulated gradient. By relaxing the gradient, the fluctuations dissipate energy, thereby causing a resistance3,13. The characteristics of the fluctuations and their corresponding resistance depend on the dimensionality of the setup as follows.

Recent findings suggest that in one-dimensional (1D) wires, discrete relaxation events known as phase slips dominate the dynamics. Microscopically, a phase slip occurs when the magnitude of the superconducting order parameter is transiently and locally suppressed over a healing length ξ. Where the amplitude vanishes, the phase is ill-defined, allowing for phase jumps of 2π. As the order parameter recovers, the wire returns to a state with a uniform amplitude but a reduced phase gradient4 (Fig. 1a, top row).

a, Dissipation in a narrow, quasi-1D channel occurs because of phase slips, in which a depletion of the order parameter allows for a relaxation of the phase gradient and kinetic energy (top row). The corresponding phase (colour-coded) evolution of a phase slip in a narrow channel is plotted in the central row. In a wide, quasi-2D channel, dissipation is governed by vortex–antivortex pairs traversing the channel (bottom row). b, A transport channel of programmable width connects two superfluid reservoirs (blue). The channel is formed by two repulsive beams (green and orange), one of which is tunable by a DMD.

In a recent development, in two-dimensional (2D) geometries, such as thin films, dissipation instead arises from the nucleation and motion of topological defects known as vortices. A vortex is a point-like singularity of the phase around which the phase winds by 2π, with a small core in which the amplitude is suppressed. Driven by a current, vortices move across the film and dissipate energy. Each time a vortex traverses the sample, the phase difference between the contacts relaxes by 2π. Repeated vortex crossings generate a finite voltage and hence an effective resistance14,15 (Fig. 1a, bottom row). In intermediate, thin-strip geometries, both vortex flow and phase slips may contribute to dissipation.

Previous studies included experiments on superconducting rings16; Dayem-bridge nanowires17,18,19,20; Bose–Einstein condensates in dumbbell21,22, cylindrical23 or toroidal geometries24; optical lattices25,26; and fermionic Josephson junctions27,28,29. These previous studies have explored various facets of phase-slip and vortex physics, including direct imaging of vortices28,30,31,32, the Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless phase transition33 and the recent observation of Shapiro steps in atomic Josephson junctions34,35. However, the experimental challenge of isolating and characterizing geometric or dimensional effects on dissipation remains unresolved.

With the rise of quantum simulation of devices based on highly controllable ultracold atomic gases36,37, it is now possible to shed new light on how these dissipative processes emerge in quantum systems.

It has been revealed that in this work, we use ultracold, strongly interacting fermions in a two-terminal configuration to study nonlinear transport through a digitally programmable channel. The optically shaped channel can be reproducibly tuned from a quasi-1D to a quasi-2D geometry, providing a platform ideally suited for probing the influence of geometry on fluctuation-driven dissipation in the absence of defects or impurities.

In the narrow, 1D channel limit, we identify signatures of phase slips, in agreement with the Langer–Ambegaokar–McCumber–Halperin (LAMH) theory4,38,39. In particular, we observe the predicted exponential suppression of the LAMH activation factor over many orders of magnitude on widening the channel. For even larger widths, the system crosses over to a 2D regime in which dissipation is dominated by vortices, as indicated by the observed power-law dependence of the current–voltage characteristics predicted for vortex dynamics.

Beyond establishing these limiting behaviours, our measurements provide a direct window into the crossover between 1D and 2D transport, a regime in which analytical modelling is challenging. It is in this crossover that widening the channel paradoxically increases its resistance. More broadly, our results highlight the utility of ultracold atomic superfluids as a platform for quantum simulation of nonequilibrium transport.

Recent findings suggest that we prepare a balanced mixture of the lowest and third-lowest hyperfine states of fermionic 6Li in the unitary regime. A total of 2N = 2.7 ± 0.1 × 105 atoms are cooled to T/TF = 0.144 ± 0.007, where N denotes the number of atom pairs, TF denotes the Fermi temperature, and the errors in both quantities denote the uncertainties due to shot-to-shot fluctuations. The temperature corresponds to T/TC ≈ 0.7, where TC ≈ 0.2TF denotes the critical temperature40. The atoms are confined in a cigar-shaped, harmonic trap with trapping frequencies (νx, νy, νz) = (222 ± 7, 28.1 ± 0.1, 195 ± 5) Hz.

Recent findings suggest that as shown in Fig. 1a, a repulsive TEM0,1 beam, propagating in the x-direction, is aligned with the trap centre. It divides the atomic cloud into two reservoirs, separated by a quasi-2D transport region that is 51 ± 1 μm long and provides confinement of ν2D = 10.46 ± 0.09 kHz along z. Within the central 27 ± 0.5 μm of this plane, the atoms are further confined in the x-direction to a channel of variable width w. The channel is defined by a repulsive beam propagating along z, shaped by a digital micromirror device (DMD). It enables reproducible tunability of w from 0.9 ± 0.5 μm to 19.8 ± 0.5 μm, in which the uncertainty is dominated by and calculated from the resolution limit of our projection system (numerical aperture = 0.53, λ = 532 nm). Note that given the dimensions of our setup, we are not in the Josephson regime (see Methods, ‘No Josephson oscillations’). A third, attractive Gaussian beam (not shown) illuminates the transport channel and its connections to the reservoirs, locally increasing the degeneracy. A more detailed description of this effect as well as of the overall setup can be found in ref. 41.

At time t = 0, we prepare a relative atom-pair imbalance between the two reservoirs, ΔN/N = (Nl − Nr)/(Nl + Nr), where Nl,r denote the number of atom pairs in the left and right reservoirs. An initial imbalance of ΔN/N ≈ 0.1 relaxes through an approximately constant initial current, followed by damped oscillations of the imbalance. The discharge is distinctly non-exponential, indicating a nonlinear response. The damping, and in particular its dependence on the channel width w, carries information about the underlying microscopic mechanisms.

In a recent development, the key data of our measurement series are shown in Fig. 2a. We record transport traces for w between 0.9 ± 0.5 μm and 19.8 ± 0.5 μm. As w increases, the magnitude of the initial current increases, which manifests in a steeper initial slope. Concurrently, both the oscillation frequency and amplitude grow. The frequency rises from just below 10 Hz to approximately 18 Hz (see also Extended Data Fig. 1). For the narrowest channel (w = 0.9 ± 0.5 μm), the oscillation amplitude is comparable to the noise floor and barely resolved. By contrast, for the widest channel (w = 19.8 ± 0.5 μm), the amplitude reaches ΔN/N ≈ 0.06.

a, Atom transport (imbalance ΔN/N as a function of time t) of a unitary Fermi gas through channels of increasing width highlights distinctively changing dissipation characteristics. The data are compared with fitted phase slip (LAMH) and vortex models. The models both describe the TNR in the circuit (b), capturing either phase slips or vortices. The LAMH model fits narrow channels, whereas the vortex model fits wide channels. The measurements for different channel widths are vertically offset for clarity. The statistical uncertainties of the measurements (typically four to five measurements per data point) are smaller than the marker size. c, A quality-of-fit \({\chi }_{\nu }^{2}\) analysis substantiates the change of the dominant model apparent in a.

According to recent reports, the damping exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on w. At longer transport times (for example, t = 0.3 s), the remaining oscillation amplitude reaches a maximum for intermediate channel widths (see also Fig. 4). These signals suggest distinct dissipative mechanisms in the narrow and wide channel limits, which we analyse quantitatively below.

According to recent reports, the general characteristics of the dynamics can be understood as arising from the interplay between the potential energy stored in the reservoirs, the kinetic energy inside the channel and the dissipative processes we want to investigate. To study these dissipative processes, we model our system with an equivalent RLC circuit shown in Fig. 2b. We first characterize the capacitance and inductance of the circuit to subsequently infer the dissipative (resistive) processes by fitting the dynamics of the circuit to the measurements. The capacitances, inductance and resistance in the circuit model correspond to the compressibility of the atomic reservoirs, the inertia of the atoms and the dissipative processes in the channel, respectively. We explore these elements in the following starting with the capacitors. As the model circuit features two capacitors in series, each with a capacitance C, the effective capacitance of the circuit is Ceff = C/2. The compressibility κeff of the gas allows to quantify this equivalent capacitance Ceff (potential energy per atom pair displaced from equilibrium) through \(\frac{1}{2}{(\Delta N/2)}^{2}/{\kappa }_{\mathrm{eff}}=\Delta {E}_{\mathrm{pot}}\equiv \frac{1}{2}{(\Delta N/2)}^{2}/{C}_{\mathrm{eff}}\). We measured the compressibility of our sample (Methods, ‘Derivation of the reservoir capacitance’) to find hCeff = 15.8 ± 0.5 s, where h is Planck’s constant. Next we quantify the inductance. To do so, we assume all channels have box-like potentials. A charge-neutral atom-pair current I carries a kinetic energy Ekin that depends on w. We define the inductance of our systems using \({E}_{{\rm{kin}}}\equiv \frac{1}{2}L{I}^{2}.\) We developed a model that predicts a functional dependence.

In a recent development, (Methods, ‘Derivation of the inductance’). By analysing the oscillation frequencies observed in our measurements and noting that in a weakly damped circuit, the frequencies are given by \(\omega (w)\approx 1/\sqrt{L(w){C}_{\mathrm{eff}}}\), we find ℓc/h = 3.01 ± 0.03 × 10−5 μm s and Lres/h = 3.06 ± 0.04 × 10−6 s. Although the details are provided in the Supplementary Information, here we state that the first term in equation (1) captures the kinetic energy in the channel, whereas the second term accounts for the kinetic energy in the reservoirs.

Phase slips and vortices dissipate the kinetic energy of the current into heat. So, they effectively act as a topological nonlinear resistor (TNR). With L and C determined, the resistance R remains the sole unknown component in our circuit. Owing to the nature of phase slips, R is topological and nonlinear, meaning it depends not only on the geometry but also on the current.

Showing how R depends on geometry, in particular in relation to the length scale given by ξ ≈ 1.2 μm (Methods, ‘Estimate of ξ’), reveals the nature of the underlying dissipative processes. To do so, we fit the width-dependent resistance R(w) in the equations of motion of an RLC circuit (derived in Methods, ‘RLC circuit modelling and fitting’).

Industry observers note that for narrow, quasi-1D channels (w ≱ 2ξ), we expect the system to be in the phase slip regime. The LAMH model predicts4.

Recent findings suggest that defined using R = V/I, where R0 is the characteristic resistance, w0 is the characteristic width, and I0 = 2kBT/h, where kB is the Boltzmann’s constant and T is the temperature. The exponential suppression of R with w reflects the thermally activated phase-slip rate scaling with \(\varGamma \propto \exp (-\Delta F/({k}_{{\rm{B}}}T))\) (ref. 18), where the free energy barrier for phase slips is ΔF ∝ w. The sinh(I/I0) term can intuitively be understood as follows: at small |I/I0| ≪ 1, phase slips occur in both directions with roughly equal probability; as the bias increases slightly, phase slips that relax the current become more probable. For large |I/I0| ≫ 1, sinh(I/I0) ≈ exp(I/I0)/2. reflecting the local destabilization of the superfluid and the resulting exponential increase in the phase-slip probability.

It has been revealed that using our predetermined C and L(w), we determine R0 and w0 by fitting them simultaneously to the measurements of our four narrowest channels (Methods, ‘RLC circuit modelling and fitting’). Assuming that the LAMH model can be used to describe our system, a simultaneous fit to multiple channel widths provides a robust extraction of the model parameters but enforces the predicted exponential suppression of RLAMH with w. We find R0/h = 102.3±0.2 and w0 = 49.7(6) nm, where the errors denote the uncertainties of the fit. The resulting fits (shown in Fig. 2a) largely capture the dynamics for channels with a width up to w = 2.5 μm. This is quantified by \(\mathrm{NRMSE}\,=\) \(\sqrt{{\sum }_{i}{({m}_{i}-{f}_{i})}^{2}/N}/({m}_{\max }-{m}_{\min }) < 0.06\), where mi and fi denote the measured and fitted imbalances, respectively, and mmax − mmin is the measured signal range. However, the \({\chi }_{\nu }^{2}\) analysis \(({\chi }_{\nu }^{2}\lesssim 9)\) shown in Fig. 2c suggests additional systematic effects beyond the very small statistical uncertainties of the measurements (typically on the level of 0.004). These systematic effects could originate from the approximation of modelling the channel with a box-like potential or the attractive beam illuminating the channel locally increasing the temperature. Outside the validity range of the model, the quality of the fits degrades noticeably, failing to capture the phase of the oscillations and underestimating their damping.

It has been revealed that in a second step, we validate the choice of the LAMH model by fitting RLAMH(w) to each curve individually. In contrast to the simultaneous fit, these individual fits do not enforce the predicted scaling RLAMH(w) and therefore provide an independent test of whether the scaling is present in the data. Within the validity regime of the model, the individual fits reproduce the predicted exponential scaling over many orders of magnitude, as shown in Fig. 3a.

Industry observers note that a, The fitted phase-slip resistance RLAMH(w), for narrow channels, shows the exponential suppression with width, as predicted by LAMH theory. b, The fitted vortex resistivity ρv(w), for wide channels, shows the predicted power law. Inside the crossover region (2–4ξ), that is, outside the validity range of the models, both scalings break down (Methods, ‘Breakdown of scaling laws’). Note that a and b display different quantities (resistance compared with resistivity) characterizing different regimes (1D compared with 2D) and are therefore not intended to be compared across the dimensional crossover. The error bars represent the error of the fit.

This is the first main finding of this paper. Compared with RLAMH(w), the total resistance R(I, w) apparent in the measurements (Fig. 2a) varies much less. As we initialize a fixed potential bias in our system, the exponential geometric suppression (R ∝ exp(−w/w0)) approximately cancels the current-induced exponential enhancement (R ∝ sinh(I/I0) ≈ exp(I/I0)/2). This allows RLAMH to be inferred over a wide range—more than 10 decades—while only exploring a relatively modest dynamic range of R. Importantly, the observed scaling of RLAMH(w) is contained within the data itself and is not just an artefact of the choice of the model. This becomes evident when the model is applied outside its validity regime, where the scaling breaks down immediately (Methods, ‘Breakdown of scaling laws’).

In quasi-2D channels (w ≳ 4ξ), phase slips become energetically unfavourable, as their activation energy increases exponentially with w. Instead, dissipation is expected to be governed by vortex flow. Owing to the vortices, we expect to see a power-law dependence in the pair-current density J:.

Recent findings suggest that where J0 = I0/ξ. A derivation, building on the results of ref. 5, is provided in the Methods, ‘Vortices in a finite width’. By fitting α and \({\widetilde{R}}_{0}\) simultaneously to the data of our four widest channels (Methods, ‘RLC circuit modelling and fitting’), we find \(\alpha =1.98\pm 0.04,{\mathop{R}\limits^{ \sim }}_{0}/h=1{0}^{-4.79\pm 0.07}\). As apparent from Fig. 2a, this model captures the dynamics for channels in the 2D regime (NRMSE ≱ 0.06). In these cases, \({\chi }_{\nu }^{2}\lesssim 4\). Note that the vortex model does not contain an explicit temperature dependence, and for wide channels, the box-potential approximation is safer compared with narrow channels. Apart from these statistical tests, we validate our model by fixing α to its global fit value but fitting ρv to each individual curve. Within the validity range of the model, these individual fits agree with the predicted power-law ρv ∝ wα−1 (Fig. 3b). This scaling is the second main finding of the paper. The scaling breaks down outside the validity regime of the model (Methods, ‘Breakdown of scaling laws’), providing evidence that the observed scaling is a feature of the data, not a mere artefact of the enforced power law R ∝ Jα−1. When approaching the dimensional crossover w ≱ 4ξ, while still largely capturing the dynamics, the model begins to slightly but systematically underestimate the amplitude of the oscillations at long times. Presumably, because the approximation of sufficiently large w used in the derivation of R(J) ceases to hold (Methods, ‘Vortices in a finite width’). The eventual breakdown of the vortex model at w ≈ 4ξ marks the end of the 2D regime: the vortex model should be valid only when vortex–antivortex pairs are available as excitations. As each vortex has a radius of ξ, such an excitation requires w ≳ 4ξ. This leaves a gap between the validity ranges of the phase slip and the vortex model, in which neither model provides a microscopically satisfactory description. In this gap, there is a dimensional crossover, in which both phase slips and vortices compete.

In a recent development, the underdamped oscillations allow us to characterize dissipation in our system using only a few basic assumptions, while staying agnostic to the dissipation mechanism. This is particularly useful to analyse the dimensional crossover, in which neither the phase-slip nor the vortex model provide a satisfactory microscopical description. We split the total energy Etot into a potential (capacitive) energy EC and a kinetic (inductive) energy EL. We assume Etot = EC(ΔN) + EL(I, w) with EC ∝ ΔN2 and EL(I = 0, w) = 0. For each channel width w, we extract the times ti,w at which ΔN(t = ti, w) reaches an extremum and thus I ≈ 0. There, the system has minimal inductive energy (EL ≈ 0) and maximal capacitive energy. The fraction of the initial energy remaining in the system is then given by.

In a recent development, the remaining energy as a function of time and channel width is shown in Fig. 4. The plot is obtained by cubic interpolation between the measured points, performed linearly in time and logarithmically in width.

Recent findings suggest that the remaining energy in the oscillator paradoxically varies non-monotonically as a function of the channel width w. For a given time after the initial decay, the maximum appears in the crossover region, near w = 4 μm ≈ 3ξ, in which phase slips and vortices are suppressed but competing. The crosses mark the measurement points (typically four to five measurements per cross) between which we interpolate. We estimate the individual data points to have a typical positive bias of 0.5% and a statistical uncertainty smaller than 2% (Methods, ‘Error estimation’).

Sources indicate that for a fixed width, the energy decays over time, reflecting dissipation. At any given time t > 0.15 s, Et(w)/E0 varies non-monotonically with the channel width, exhibiting a clear maximum near w ≈ 3ξ, corresponding to a minimal effective resistance. We call this deviation from the expected monotonicity the ‘quantum resistance paradox’ and consider it the third and last main finding of this paper. Note that the activation energy for phase slips increases exponentially with channel width, whereas vortex–antivortex pairs require sufficiently wide channels to form. The observed non-monotonicity thus suggests a transition in the underlying dissipation mechanism and a crossover from 1D to 2D physics.

Sources indicate that we have investigated atom transport between two bulk superfluids through channels across different dimensional regimes and observed distinct behaviours. In narrow, quasi-1D channels, our data are in agreement with those of the LAMH model. We infer the geometric suppression of the phase slips by many orders of magnitude, providing the first experimental confirmation of the predicted geometric scaling. For wide, quasi-2D channels, dissipation is captured by a vortex flow model. The borders of the 1D and 2D regimes appear close to the theoretically expected length scale. A measurement of energy decay, agnostic to microscopic details, provides further evidence for a transition in the dissipation mechanism for channels of intermediate width, which paradoxically exhibit the least energy loss. These findings not only suggest routes for optimizing energy transport in mesoscopic devices but also provide a benchmark for theoretical efforts to describe the delicate phase-slip and vortex-flow mechanisms in the dimensional crossover in superfluids and superconductors42,43,44.

Our setup is analogous to an RLC circuit with the mapping presented in Extended Data Table 1.

The procedures for determining the capacitance C and the inductance L are described in sections ‘Derivation of the reservoir capacitance’ and ‘Derivation of the inductance’. Here, we derive the governing equations and provide additional details on the fitting procedure used to determine R, as presented in the main text.

Recent findings suggest that the total number of atoms in each reservoir is measured directly using absorption images of both hyperfine states (|1⟩ and |3⟩), taken in rapid succession. To determine the total number of pairs in each reservoir Nl,r, we use both measurements, as this reduces statistical uncertainty. Specifically, \({N}_{{\rm{l}},{\rm{r}}}=({N}_{{\rm{l}},{\rm{r}};|1\rangle }+{N}_{{\rm{l}},{\rm{r}};|3\rangle })/2\), where \({N}_{{\rm{l}},{\rm{r}};|i\rangle }\) denotes the number of atoms in the left and right reservoirs in state |i⟩. However, the second image (state |3⟩) demonstrates a cloud that has absorbed some energy from the first imaging pulse and is therefore slightly distorted. To avoid systematic effects from this distortion on C and T, we use only the image of the lowest hyperfine state (|1⟩) to extract the compressibility and temperature of the cloud, assuming these are identical for both states. We verified that our preparation is equivalent for both states by inverting the imaging sequence. We describe our system in terms of pairs and report C, L and R for pairs and pair currents, respectively.

With this replacement, we obtain a standard RLC series circuit with an initially charged capacitor but no externally applied voltage.

Applying Kirchhoff’s voltage law and charge conservation, we find.
